statement:
The intrinsic coefficient module and its residue complex. The finite locally constant sheaves $\mathcal K_n=\mathcal K/3^n$
on $X$ satisfy
\[
 H^i(X,\mathcal K_n)=0\quad(i\ge2),\qquad
 |H^1(X,\mathcal K_n)|=3^{23n}|H^0(X,\mathcal K_n)|.
 \tag{A.1.1}
\]
Their degree-one cohomology groups are finite. For every finite set
$J$ of primes different from three there is a compatible distinguished
triangle in the derived category of abelian groups
\[
 R\Gamma(X,\mathcal K_n)\longrightarrow
 R\Gamma(X\setminus J,\mathcal K_n)\longrightarrow
 \bigoplus_{q\in J}R\Gamma(\mathbb F_q,\mathcal K_n(-1))[-1]
 \longrightarrow R\Gamma(X,\mathcal K_n)[1].
 \tag{A.1.2}
\]
Every $D_q$ is injective and has finite cokernel. Localization and
continuous cochains induce isomorphisms
\[
 H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathcal K)
       \simeq\mathcal R(A)/D\mathcal R(A),
 \qquad
 H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathcal K)
       \simeq H^1_{\rm cts}(G_S,\mathcal K).
 \tag{A.1.3}
\]
The latter group is finitely generated of rank $23$; its torsion is
$H^0(G_S,(\mathcal K\otimes\mathbb Q_3)/\mathcal K)$.
This is an exact residue calculation, including the contribution over
$\mathbb Z[1/3]$ in the degrees relevant to lifting sections.

 \longrightarrow\frac{\mathcal R(A)}{D\mathcal R(A)}
 \longrightarrow
 \varprojlim_n\bigoplus_{q\ne3}\operatorname{coker}(D_q\bmod3^n)

\]

statement:
A linear family inside the nonabelian lifting problem. The pullback is an exact sequence of continuous Galois lattices
\[
 0\longrightarrow\mathcal K\longrightarrow E_w
 \longrightarrow\mathbb Z_3(1)\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{A.3.2}
\]
Choose an integral lift $l$ of the standard generator, and after
twisting put
\[
 u_q=F_q(l\otimes1)-l\otimes1\in A_q.
 \tag{A.3.3}
\]
For $a=(a_p)_p\in\mathcal R_{\mathbb P}(\mathbb Z_3)$, the section
$\ell\circ\kappa(a)$ of $N^{\rm cc}\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$ has
obstruction represented, under (A.1.3), by
\[
 (a_qu_q)_{q\ne3}.
 \tag{A.3.4}
\]
Its unique possible local corrections are $-a_qD_q^{-1}u_q$.
Thus it lifts precisely when these corrections are integral and
form a restricted family. Changing $l$ changes (A.3.4) by $D$ of
a restricted family.
For the families used below, $a_3=0$. In E24's pro-three coordinates
and the E36 generator $k=-\delta$, their actual torsor coordinates
are
\[
 \alpha:\quad(r_1,r_2;A,B,C)=(0,-\kappa(a);
                  -\kappa(a),-\kappa(a),-\kappa(a)),
 \qquad a_{\rm E36}=-a.
 \tag{A.3.5}
\]
The three $K_0$ coordinates use the inclusion of rational Kummer
classes; the other torsion, framed-$\lambda$, and divisible
coordinates are zero. This specifies the pairs themselves in the
requested convention.

The full class-two residue criterion in based cusp-path coordinates. Choose geometric paths from the specified tangent at $O$ to a
Galois-equivariant family of tangents at the nine cusps. Let $c_d$
be the corresponding inertia elements in $N/\gamma_3N$ and
$b_{g,d}\in V$ their abelian comparison cochains, with convention
\[
 g(\log c_d)=\chi(g)\bigl(\log c_{gd}
                         -b_{g,d}\wedge e_{gd}\bigr).
 \tag{A.8.1}
\]
For a continuous representative $s$ of a class in
$\operatorname{Sec}(N^{\rm cc})$, write
\[
 \log s(\tau_q)=\sum_{d\in D}t_{q,d}c_d,\quad
 v_q=\alpha(\phi_q),\quad
 w_q=\sum_dt_{q,d}e_d\in W.
 \tag{A.8.2}
\]
Here $s(\tau_q)$ means its geometric cocycle value, the chosen
arithmetic action is unramified at $q$, and $\phi_q\tau_q\phi_q^{-1}
=\tau_q^q$. Then its full intrinsic obstruction is represented by
the restricted family
\[
 r_q=v_q\wedge w_q-
            \sum_dt_{q,d}\,b_{\phi_q,d}\wedge e_{\phi_qd}
       \in\mathcal K(-1).
 \tag{A.8.3}
\]
The section lifts exactly when
\[
 -D_q^{-1}r_q\in A_q\quad\text{for all }q\ne3,
 \qquad (-D_q^{-1}r_q)_q\in\mathcal R(A).
 \tag{A.8.4}
\]
The nonempty fibres are exactly the torsors in A.7.

$\phi_{\mathfrak q}$ on $Q$. Sections unramified outside

\[
 \operatorname{Sec}_{\{3,7\}}(Q)\simeq
 \{(a,b)\in Q^2:aF(b)a^{-1}=b^7\}/Q^c,
 \tag{A.15.1}
\]
where
\[
 h\cdot(a,b)=\bigl(h^{-1}aF(h),\ h^{-1}bh\bigr)
       \quad(h\in Q^c).
 \tag{A.15.2}
\]
The parameterization is natural under all the quotient maps.
For a surjective equivariant morphism $R\twoheadrightarrow Q$
among these geometric pro-three groups, a class represented by
$(a,b)$ lifts exactly when there are lifts $A,B\in R$ satisfying
\[
 A F(B)A^{-1}=B^7.
 \tag{A.15.3}
\]
The same statement holds for $R=N$. Moreover a fixed class-two
section supported at these primes lifts to $N$ exactly when
it lifts to every lower-central quotient $N/\gamma_rN$.
The equivalence includes compatible full lifts; no compatibility

The complete local metabelian image at every good prime. Let $k/\mathbb Q_q$ be finite with $q\ne3$, put
$Q=N/N''$, and retain the unit tangential origin at $O$.
Every continuous section of $Q\rtimes G_k$ is either

when its abelianization is unramified.

More precisely, with $F$ denoting the reference arithmetic

the local section set is the disjoint union
\[
 \operatorname{Sec}_k(Q)=
 Q/\{a\sim h^{-1}aF(h):h\in Q\}
 \ \sqcup\!
 \coprod_{d\in D(k)}
 \{u\in k^{\times\wedge_3}:v_k(u)\ne0\}.
 \tag{A.19.1}
\]
The first term consists of unramified sections, with $a$

      \simeq\mathbb Z_3\oplus
                 \mu_{3^{v_3(Q_k-1)}}(k).
\]
The morphism
$\operatorname{Sec}_k(N)\to\operatorname{Sec}_k(Q)$

The ramified image of

 B/\{x\sim h^{-1}x\,u(h):h\in B^c\}.                 \tag{A.20.1}
\]

The fiber over the class represented by $x$ in (A.20.1) is
\[
 p^{-1}(x)/\{y\sim h^{-1}y\,u(h):h\in J^c\}.        \tag{A.20.2}
\]
These orbit sets specify all identifications between the lifts.

statement:
Cofinality and the exact comparison of section limits. For every number field $L$ and each specified $R$, the natural
maps are an isomorphism of pro-three groups and a bijection of
pointed sets, respectively:
\[
 Q_R\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{r\ge3}Q_{R,r},\qquad
 H^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_L,Q_R)\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \varprojlim_{r\ge3}H^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_L,Q_{R,r}).    \tag{A.21.1}
\]
Each $Q_{R,r}$ has a finite central series of finitely generated
$\mathbb Z_3$-module factors, and every finite quotient of $Q_R$
factors through one of them. They are cofinal finite-rank
quotients for this section problem.

statement:
Metabelian coefficient lattices and the next lifting fiber. For $r\ge2$ put $M_r=\gamma_r(N/N'')/\gamma_{r+1}(N/N'')$.
There is a natural $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant isomorphism
\[
 M_r\simeq\ker\bigl(V\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^{r-1}V
             \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^rV\bigr),\qquad
 \operatorname{rank}M_r=(r-1)\binom{r+8}{r},             \tag{A.22.1}
\]
where the arrow is multiplication. For $r\ge3$, write
$A_{r,q}=M_r(-1)$ and $D_{r,q}=\operatorname{Frob}_q-1$.
Then
\[
\begin{split}
 H^2_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q},M_r)
   &=\mathcal R(A_r)/D_r\mathcal R(A_r),\\
 \varprojlim{}^1H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},M_r/3^n)
   &=\frac{\mathcal R(A_r)\cap\prod_{q\ne3}D_{r,q}A_{r,q}}
           {D_r\mathcal R(A_r)}\ne0,\\
 H^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(G_{\mathbb Q},M_r)
   &=M_r/(u-1)M_r^c.
\end{split}
\tag{A.22.2}
\]
The matrices on $M_r$ are the kernel functor (A.22.1) applied
to the explicit matrices on $V$ in A.7, giving a finite integral
prescription for every first-cohomology Smith factor.

The next coefficient of the full, metabelian, and marked
depth-two towers is the same rank-$330$ lattice $M_3$, and
\[
\begin{split}
 H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},M_3)\simeq\mathbb Z_3^{166}
 &\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)^7\oplus(\mathbb Z/9)^{56}\\
 &\oplus(\mathbb Z/27)^{25}\oplus(\mathbb Z/81)^3.
\end{split}
\tag{A.22.3}
\]
Every nonempty lifting fiber from class two to class three is
a torsor under (A.22.3).

statement:
The complete one-prime metabelian image and its fibers for $q\in\Sigma$. For each $q\in\Sigma$ of A.16, put $S_q=\{3,q,\infty\}$.
Then
\[
 \operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N/N'')
       \quad\text{is surjective}.
 \tag{A.24.1}
\]
For either $B=N$ or $B=N/N''$, the exact image in class
two is
\[
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(B)
                  \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr)
   =\operatorname{res}_q^{-1}(\mathscr L_q).
 \tag{A.24.2}
\]
All fibers are as follows. A target outside the displayed
subset has empty fiber. A target unramified at $q$ has
precisely the unramified fiber of (A.20.2); every lift in
the present fiber is unramified outside three. For a target
whose restriction at $q$ is ramified and belongs to
$\mathscr L_q$, choosing one normalized lift gives a
bijection of its fiber with the set of right cosets
\[
                         J_B/J_B^c.
 \tag{A.24.3}
\]
Here $J_B^c$ is the fixed subgroup of the actual complex
conjugation, and it is not asserted to be normal.
The same description for the ramified fibers of
(A.24.1) is $N''/(N'')^c$.

statement:
The relative arithmetic presentation at every inert prime $q\equiv2,5\pmod9$. Put
\[
 \Xi=\{q\text{ prime}:q\equiv2\text{ or }5\pmod9\}.
 \tag{A.25.1}
\]
This set has natural density $1/3$ and contains $2$.
For $q\in\Xi$ let $\mathfrak q=(q)$ be the unique
prime of $K_0$ above $q$, and write
$P_q=G_{K_0,\{\lambda,\mathfrak q,\infty\}}(3)$.
After conjugating the local embedding compatibly with
the fixed global complex conjugation, there is an
isomorphism
\[
 P_q\simeq D_{q^2}*_{3}\mathbb Z_3^{\langle z\rangle},
 \qquad
 D_{q^2}=\langle\phi,\tau\mid
                  \phi\tau\phi^{-1}=\tau^{q^2}\rangle_3,
 \tag{A.25.2}
\]
and its relative arithmetic quotient is
\[
 \Gamma_q\simeq
 (D_{q^2}*_{3}\mathbb Z_3^{\langle z\rangle})
                   \rtimes\langle c\rangle,
 \qquad
 c\phi c^{-1}=\phi,\quad
 c\tau c^{-1}=\tau^{-1},\quad czc^{-1}=z^{-1}.
 \tag{A.25.3}
\]
Here $c^2=1$. Thus $\sigma=zc$ is another involution,
with no further relation beyond (A.25.3). The source
category in these presentations consists of profinite
groups whose kernel over $\langle c\rangle$ is pro-three;
the kernel free product is precisely the pro-three free
product, as displayed.

For an inert prime $q\equiv8\pmod9$, the two unit
Frobenius values used in this construction are both zero
modulo three. In particular $q=17$ is the smallest prime
not covered by $\Sigma\cup\Xi$; (A.25.2) is not asserted
there. The union $\Sigma\cup\Xi$ has natural density
$5/9$.
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16,
folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379).}

statement:
The complete one-prime metabelian image and fibers for $q\in\Xi$. For every $q\in\Xi$ and $S_q=\{3,q,\infty\}$,
the conclusions (A.24.1)--(A.24.2) hold. Thus every
metabelian section supported at these primes lifts
to $N$, and for $B=N$ or $N/N''$ the exact image
in class two is
\[
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(B)
                  \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr)
       =\operatorname{res}_q^{-1}(\mathscr L_q).
 \tag{A.26.1}
\]
For targets unramified at $q$, the fiber is exactly
the unramified fiber of A.20. For a ramified target
in this image, choose a normalized lift and let
$X_0$ be its cocycle value at the involution
$\sigma=zc$ of A.25. On $J_B$ put
\[
                     \Theta=\operatorname{Ad}(X_0)\circ\sigma.
\]
This is an involution. The fiber is in bijection
with either of the following explicitly identified
sets:
\[
 \{j\in J_B:j\Theta(j)=1\}
       \simeq J_B^{\Theta}\backslash J_B,
 \qquad h\longmapsto h^{-1}\Theta(h).
 \tag{A.26.2}
\]
The quotient in the right member is a set of left
cosets, without an assertion of normality. The same
ramified-fiber formula for the surjection from full
to metabelian sections uses $J_B=N''$ and the
involution supplied by the chosen full lift.

statement:
The normalized integral Frobenius at an inert prime and the explicit Heisenberg test at seventeen. Retain the free pro-three basis $u,v=cuc$ of $P_3$ from
A.10, and write $[u,v]=uvu^{-1}v^{-1}$. For an inert
rational prime $q\ne3$, conjugate its local order-two
complement in $P_3\rtimes\langle c\rangle$ to $\langle c\rangle$.
Let $\varphi_q\in P_3$ be the resulting arithmetic Frobenius
of the prime of $K_0$ of norm $q^2$. Its image in the
integral class-two quotient is exactly
\[
 \varphi_q\bmod\gamma_3P_3
       =u^{a_q}v^{a_q}[u,v]^{-a_q^2/2},
 \qquad a_q=\frac{\log(-q)}{\log7}\in\mathbb Z_3.
 \tag{A.27.1}
\]
The image in (A.27.1) is independent of the conjugator
used to identify the local order-two complement with
$\langle c\rangle$.

Put $\theta=\zeta_9$, $\beta^3=\lambda$, and
\[
 u_i=1-\zeta^i\theta\quad(0\le i\le2),\qquad
 \omega=u_1u_2^2,
 \qquad
 L=K_0(\theta,\beta,\omega^{1/3}).
 \tag{A.27.2}
\]
Then $L/K_0$ is the full exponent-three class-two
quotient of $P_3$: its Galois group has order $27$ and
presentation
\[
 \langle\sigma,\tau,\rho\mid
  \sigma^3=\tau^3=\rho^3=1,\quad
  \rho\text{ central},\quad[\sigma,\tau]=\rho\rangle.
 \tag{A.27.3}
\]
The field is Galois over $\mathbb Q$, and complex
conjugation acts by
\[
 c\sigma c=\tau\sigma,
 \qquad c\tau c=\tau^{-1},
 \qquad c\rho c=\rho^{-1}.
 \tag{A.27.4}
\]
For every prime $q\equiv8\pmod9$, the Frobenius of
the prime of $K_0$ above $q$ is trivial in (A.27.3).
In particular this holds at $17$, although
$v_3(a_{17})=1$ in the integral formula (A.27.1).
For example,
\[
 a_{17}\equiv78\pmod{81},\qquad
 -a_{17}^2/2\equiv36\pmod{81}.
 \tag{A.27.5}
\]
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16,
folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379);
the first inert prime outside A.25 in Tasks A.6 and B.4.}

statement:
The exact equivariant one-relator presentation at every inert prime. Let $q\ne3$ be any inert rational prime, and
let $P_q=G_{K_0,\{3,q\}}(3)$ and
$\Gamma_q=P_q\rtimes\langle c\rangle$.
After the local-complement identification used
in A.27, choose a tame generator $t$ and an
arithmetic Frobenius $\phi$ at the prime over
$q$, with
\[
 c(t)=t^{-1},\qquad c(\phi)=\phi,
 \qquad \phi t\phi^{-1}=t^{q^2}.
 \tag{A.28.1}
\]
Choose a lift $x\in P_q$ of $u\in P_3$ and
put $y=cxc$. The lift can and will be chosen
with $\kappa_q(x)=0$ modulo three. Let
$F=F_3(x,y,t)$ be the free pro-three group
with involution $c(x)=y$, $c(y)=x$,
$c(t)=t^{-1}$. Its natural equivariant
map to $P_q$ is surjective. There is a
$c$-fixed pro-three word $W\in F$ mapping
to the actual local Frobenius $\phi$,
and for every such choice the natural map
gives the exact presentations
\[
 \begin{split}
 P_q&\simeq
 F/\overline{\langle\!\langle
          WtW^{-1}t^{-q^2}\rangle\!\rangle},\\
 \Gamma_q&\simeq
 \bigl(F/\overline{\langle\!\langle
          WtW^{-1}t^{-q^2}\rangle\!\rangle}\bigr)
                         \rtimes\langle c\rangle.
 \end{split}
 \tag{A.28.2}
\]
These are continuous pro-three presentations,
with the indicated finite operator group in
the second line. In particular
\[
 P_q^{\mathrm{ab}}\simeq
 \mathbb Z_3^2\oplus\mathbb Z_3/(q^2-1),
 \qquad
 \dim_{\mathbb F_3}H^2(P_q,\mathbb F_3)=1.
 \tag{A.28.3}
\]
At $q=17$, $W$ lies in $\Phi(F)$, and the
relator in (A.28.2) lies in the third
Zassenhaus subgroup of $F$. Its image on
killing $t$ is the actual Frobenius of A.27;
in particular its integral class-two image
is given by (A.27.1) and (A.27.5).

For any of the geometric quotients $B$ under
consideration, (A.28.2) gives the following
exact section parameterization. Normalize
the value at $c$ to one; assign the values
$a,c(a),b$ at $x,y,t$. If
$\Omega_W(a,b)$ denotes the value at $W$
of this continuous free-group cocycle,
the remaining equations are precisely
\[
 c(b)=b^{-1},\qquad
 \Omega_W(a,b)F_{q^2}(b)\Omega_W(a,b)^{-1}
                                      =b^{q^2}.
 \tag{A.28.4}
\]
Classes are the orbits under $B^c$ acting by
\[
 (a,b)\longmapsto
       (h^{-1}a\,x(h),\ h^{-1}bh).
 \tag{A.28.5}
\]
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16,
folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379);
Tasks A.6 and B.4 beyond the prime families A.16 and A.25.}

statement:
Local cuspidality at every finite derived level and its global one-prime consequences. Write $N^{(0)}=N$ and
$N^{(m+1)}=\overline{[N^{(m)},N^{(m)}]}$,
and put $Q_m=N/N^{(m)}$ for $m\ge2$.
For every finite extension $k/\mathbb Q_q$,
$q\ne3$, every continuous section with
geometric quotient $Q_m$ is either unramified
or lies in exactly one actual cusp packet.
Its inertia is trivial exactly when its
abelian inertia is zero. Every such local
section lifts to $N$, and the map from full
to $Q_m$ sections is bijective on the
ramified classes. Thus the exact local
description in A.19 holds with $Q_m$ in
place of $N/N''$, including the actual
central Frobenius coordinates of its image
in class two.

For every $q\in\Sigma\cup\Xi$ and every
$m\ge2$, the global map
\[
 \operatorname{Sec}_{\{3,q,\infty\}}(N)
       \longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Sec}_{\{3,q,\infty\}}(Q_m)
 \tag{A.29.1}
\]
is onto. For ramified targets its fiber
is the right-coset set
$N^{(m)}/(N^{(m)})^c$ when $q\in\Sigma$,
and the left-coset set
$(N^{(m)})^\Theta\backslash N^{(m)}$
when $q\in\Xi$, with the chosen-lift
involution $\Theta$ of A.26. Unramified
fibers are the exact unramified fibers
of A.20 for the map $N\to Q_m$.

folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379);
the successive derived approximations in Tasks A.6 and B.4.}

statement:
The mixed Heisenberg test at seventeen and the exact first relation degree. Use the presentation at $q=17$ in A.28.
For its Frobenius word and defining relator,
the stronger exact conclusions are
\[
 W\in D_3(F)\setminus D_4(F),\qquad
 r=WtW^{-1}t^{-289}
           \in D_4(F)\setminus D_5(F).
 \tag{A.30.1}
\]
Here $D_n(F)$ is the Zassenhaus filtration,
equivalently the filtration by degree in
the mod-three Magnus expansion of the
free pro-three group $F=F_3(x,y,t)$.
If $x,y,t$ have Magnus variables $X,Y,T$,
the degree-four part of $r-1$ has
coefficient $2$ on both $X^3T$ and
$Y^3T$. These coefficients are
independent of the other degree-three
coefficients of $W-1$.

The arithmetic input detecting the
only possible degree-two component
of $W$ is the following explicit
Heisenberg extension. Let
\[
 \alpha^3=3,\qquad \beta^3=17,
 \qquad u_0=2+\alpha^2,
 \qquad u_i=\sigma^i(u_0),
 \quad \sigma(\alpha)=\zeta\alpha,
\]
and set
\[
 \omega=u_1u_2^2,
 \qquad L_{3,17}=K_0(\alpha,\beta,\omega^{1/3}).
 \tag{A.30.2}
\]
This field is Galois over $K_0$, has
the group (A.27.3), and is unramified
outside three and seventeen. At the
prime with $\alpha\equiv7\pmod{17}$,
the Frobenius fixing the uniformizer
roots has trivial image in the center
of this Heisenberg quotient.

the next arithmetic relation at the first remaining inert prime
in Tasks A.6 and B.4.}

statement:
The nonzero cubic Frobenius term at seventeen and its failure to be a cube. Let $L_0=K_0(\alpha)$ with $\alpha^3=3$, and
let $H=G_{L_0,\{3\}}(3)\subset P_3$.
Put
\[
 \pi=\frac{\lambda}{\alpha},\qquad
 \eta=\alpha^2-2,\qquad
 \delta=1+\zeta^2\alpha+\zeta\pi.
 \tag{A.31.1}
\]
The four Kummer classes of
$\zeta,\pi,\eta,\delta$ form an
$\mathbb F_3$-basis of $H^1(H,\mathbb F_3)$.
At every prime of $L_0$ above seventeen,
the Frobenius row on this basis is
\[
                         (0,0,0,1).
 \tag{A.31.2}
\]

Choose $m\in P_3^c$ whose abelian
coordinates in the basis $u,v$ are
$(1,1)$, and put $n=vu^{-1}$.
Then $m,n$ are a free pro-three
basis, $c(m)=m$, $c(n)=n^{-1}$,
and the normalized Frobenius
of A.27 satisfies the exact congruence
\[
 \varphi_{17}\equiv
       m^6[n,[n,m]]\pmod{D_4(P_3)}.
 \tag{A.31.3}
\]
Moreover $\varphi_{17}$ is not a cube
of any element of $P_3$.

folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379);
the explicit nonprimitive Frobenius in Tasks A.6 and B.4.}

statement:
The exact marked global image and ramified fibers on $\Sigma\cup\Xi$. Put
$R=N/\gamma_3(I_{\mathrm{mark}})$,
$A=N/\gamma_3N$, and
$J_R=\ker(R\to A)$.
For every $q\in\Sigma\cup\Xi$,
the three global class-two images
coincide and are exactly
\[
 \begin{split}
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N)
                                   \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr)
 &=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N/N'')
                                   \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr)\\
 &=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(R)
                                   \to\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(A)\bigr)
   =\operatorname{res}_q^{-1}(\mathscr L_q),
 \end{split}
 \tag{A.32.1}
\]
where $S_q=\{3,q,\infty\}$ and
$\mathscr L_q$ is the actual local
unramified and cusp-packet set of A.24.

Fix a ramified class-two target in
this image and let $d\in D(\mathbb Q_q)$
be its unique local cusp. Define its
local marked lifting-class set by
\[
 \mathcal L_{q,d}=
 \begin{cases}
  \{*\},&d\ne Q_c,\\
  \mathcal C_{\mathbb Q_q,Q_c},&d=Q_c,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{A.32.2}
\]
using exactly the reference and
quotient of B.12--B.13.
Restriction gives a surjection from
the global marked fiber onto
$\mathcal L_{q,d}$.
For each element of this local
class set, choose a normalized
global marked lift above it.
The inverse image of that element
is precisely
\[
 \begin{cases}
 J_R/J_R^c,&q\in\Sigma,\\
 J_R^\Theta\backslash J_R,&q\in\Xi,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{A.32.3}
\]
with right and left cosets,
respectively. In the second case
$\Theta=\operatorname{Ad}(X_0)\circ\sigma$
is the actual involution specified
by the chosen lift in A.26.
Thus (A.32.2)--(A.32.3) describe
the entire fiber without identifying
different local marked classes or
asserting a canonical product
decomposition. Targets unramified
at $q$ have exactly the unramified
fiber of A.20 for $R\to A$.

The exact image of
$\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(N)\to
\operatorname{Sec}_{S_q}(R)$ consists
of the classes unramified at $q$,
the unmarked ramified cusp classes,
and the marked ramified classes
whose local parameter in
$\mathcal C_{\mathbb Q_q,Q_c}$ is zero.
Its nonempty ramified fibers are
given by (A.32.3) with
$J_R$ replaced by
$\gamma_3(I_{\mathrm{mark}})$ and
the corresponding chosen full lift.
In particular there are global
marked sections supported at
$\{3,q\}$ which have no full lift,
although their class-two image
has a full lift. These examples
still have no full lift after
any finite number-field extension.

the marked higher image and fibers in Task A.6.}

statement:
A class-three lift for every finite-support locally cuspidal class-two section. Let $S'$ be any finite set of rational primes containing three,
with the real place included. Put $A=N/\gamma_3N$ and
$M_3=\gamma_3N/\gamma_4N$. Every section of $A$ over
$G_{\mathbb Q,S'}$ whose restriction at each
$q\in S'\setminus\{3\}$ belongs to the actual local image
$\mathscr L_q$ of B.8 has a section lift to $N/\gamma_4N$
over the same arithmetic group. Its lifting fiber is a torsor under
\[
 H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,S'},M_3)
 =H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M_3)
 =\mathbb Z_3^{166}\oplus(\mathbb Z/3)^7
   \oplus(\mathbb Z/9)^{56}
   \oplus(\mathbb Z/27)^{25}
   \oplus(\mathbb Z/81)^3.
 \tag{A.33.1}
\]
These assertions concern the actual common class-three quotient
of the full and metabelian groups.

There is also an exact obstruction to choosing this global lift
with prescribed actual cuspidal local class-three restrictions.
Let $J\subset S'\setminus\{3\}$ be the primes where the
class-two target is ramified. Choose any global class-three lift
$s_3$. At each $q\in J$ the unique actual cuspidal class-three
lifting class determines a difference
$\Delta_q(s_3)\in M_3/(F_q-1)M_3$. The element
\[
 \left[(\Delta_q(s_3))_{q\in J}\right]
 \in\operatorname{coker}\left(
 H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M_3)
 \xrightarrow{\operatorname{res}}
 \bigoplus_{q\in J}M_3/(F_q-1)M_3\right)
 \tag{A.33.2}
\]
is independent of $s_3$. It vanishes exactly when a global
class-three lift can have all the indicated cuspidal restrictions.
Every full or metabelian global lift of the class-two target
forces (A.33.2) to vanish.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The restriction map at seventeen and a class-three lift that stops at class four. Use the actual arithmetic generators $m,n,c$ of A.31.
On the degree-three lattice $M_3$, the restriction map
\[
 H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},M_3)
 \longrightarrow H^1(G_{\mathbb Q_{17}},M_3)
                         =M_3/(F_{17}-1)M_3
 \tag{A.34.1}
\]
has image of dimension $15$ after reduction in the local
target modulo three. The target modulo three has dimension
$164$, and the cokernel of (A.34.1) modulo three therefore
has dimension $149$.

Fix free geometric generators $x_0,\ldots,x_9$ whose
abelianizations are the integral basis of A.7, with the
first eight entries the non-$O$ cusp generators. In $M_3$
put $e=[[x_8,x_0],x_9]$. The exact normalized cocycle
\[
 \beta(c)=0,\qquad \beta(m)=(1+c)e,
                  \qquad\beta(n)=0
 \tag{A.34.2}
\]
is unramified outside three. Start with the actual full
$O$-cuspidal section whose tangent parameter is $17$,
project it to $N/\gamma_4N$, and twist by $\beta$.
The resulting global section $s_3$ has the same class-two
image as that full cuspidal section, but $s_3$ has no lift
to $N/\gamma_5N$. In particular it has no full or
metabelian lift, and no lift to the marked quotient with
marked cusp $Q_c$.

Thus a class-two target with a full lift can have a
class-three lifting class with a nonzero next obstruction.
The theorem does not assert non-lifting of that class-two
target: its original full cuspidal lift is specified above.

rank fifteen. The exact prescriptions

 \gamma_B(c)=0,\qquad \gamma_B(m)=0,
                  \qquad\gamma_B(n)=B
 \tag{A.35.1}

define an unramified-outside-three class-two central cocycle.
Twist the class-two image of the global $O$-cuspidal section
with tangent parameter $17$ by $\gamma_B$.
Its restriction at seventeen is the same actual class-two
cusp section, including its Frobenius coordinate. This target
has a global class-three lift with unchanged local inertia.
For the exact gluing class (A.33.2), its image in the

statement:
Miller covers and their two exact norm comparisons at seven. The Fermat curve in the task has the following specified isomorphism
with the minimal Weierstrass curve $E_m:y_m^2+y_m=x_m^3-7$:
\[
 x_m=\frac{-3z}{x+y},\quad
 y_m=\frac{4x-5y}{x+y},\qquad
 [x:y:z]=[y_m+5:4-y_m:-3x_m].                 \tag{A.36.1}
\]
It carries $O$ to the Weierstrass origin and carries
$P,Q_c$ to $(3,-5),(3,4)$, respectively.
All of $E_m[9]$ is defined over the unramified degree-three
extension of $\Q_7$. Its reduction over
$k=\F_7[\theta]/(\theta^3-2)$ has exactly 81 points.
One point above $P$ under multiplication by three is
\[
 Q=(2+\theta^2,\ 1+\theta+6\theta^2),\qquad
 \varphi Q-Q=(6,2),                           \tag{A.36.2}
\]
where $\varphi$ raises the residue coordinates to their seventh
powers. The unique nine-torsion lifts give the corresponding
identities over the unramified local extension.

For each of the nine points $Q$ above either $d=P$ or $d=Q_c$,
let $v_R=x_m-x_m(R)$ and let $\ell_{R,S}$ be the line through
$R,S$, tangent at $R$ when $R=S$, normalized to have
$y_m$ coefficient one. Then the actual function
\[
 a_Q=\frac{\ell_{Q,Q}\ell_{2Q,Q}}{v_{2Q}v_d},\qquad
 \operatorname{div}(a_Q)=3(Q)-(d)-2(O),        \tag{A.36.3}
\]
defines a connected cubic cover $w^3=a_Q$ which is finite
\'etale over $U$. Its geometric character is an explicit
Kummer class with nonzero cusp valuations at $d,O$.
With $\iota(R)=-R$, the following function identities hold:
\[
 a_Q\,\iota^*a_Q=\frac{(x_m-x_m(Q))^3}{x_m-x_m(d)},
 \qquad
 \prod_{i=0}^2 a_{\varphi^iQ}=g_Q^3.           \tag{A.36.4}
\]
In the second identity, put $Q_i=\varphi^iQ$,
$S=Q_0+Q_1$, and
\[
       g_Q=\frac{\ell_{Q_0,Q_1}\ell_{S,Q_2}}{v_Sv_d}.
                                                        \tag{A.36.5}
\]
This function is defined over $\Q_7$, and its reduction is
defined over $\F_7$.

For the exact Fermat parameter $s=z/x$ and its unit tangent,
the regularized constants are
\[
 (s^2a_Q)(O)=9,
 \qquad (s^2(x_m-3))(O)=(s^2(x_m-3\zeta^2))(O)=9.
                                                        \tag{A.36.6}
\]
In the large model $Y^2=X^3-432$, $X=4x_m$, $Y=8y_m+4$,
the corresponding normalized Miller function is $4a_Q$,
with regularized constant 36. For the residue embedding
$\zeta\mapsto2\in\F_7$, the cubic residue of 9 is
$4=\zeta^2$, whereas that of 36 is 1.
These are arithmetic cover data; no central Galois action
on an intrinsic Heisenberg quotient is inferred from them.

statement:
An order-eighty-one arithmetic quotient and a tame-letter Frobenius coefficient at seventeen. Put $K_0=\mathbb Q(\zeta)$, $\zeta^2+\zeta+1=0$, and
$L_{17}=K_0(\beta)$ with $\beta^3=17$. Let
$\sigma(\beta)=\zeta\beta$ and set
\[
 \delta=\frac{-7-\zeta-3\beta-\beta^2}{3},\qquad
 \delta_i=\sigma^i(\delta),\qquad
 r_i^3=\delta_i\quad(i\in\mathbb Z/3).
 \tag{A.37.1}
\]
The extension
\[
 M_{17}=L_{17}(r_0,r_1,r_2)/K_0
 \tag{A.37.2}
\]
is Galois, unramified outside three and seventeen, with group
\[
 G=(\mathbb F_3)^3\rtimes\langle s\rangle,
 \qquad s^3=1,
 \tag{A.37.3}
\]
where $s(r_i)=r_{i+1}$ and $s(\beta)=\zeta\beta$.
For $a=(a_0,a_1,a_2)$ write
$\tau_a(r_i)=\zeta^{a_i}r_i$, $\tau_a(\beta)=\beta$.
Then
$s\tau_as^{-1}=\tau_{Sa}$, where $(Sa)_i=a_{i-1}$.
The group has order $81$, lower-central orders
$81,9,3,1$, exponent nine, and trivial fourth
three-Zassenhaus subgroup.

Use the arithmetic generators $m,n,t$ of A.28 and A.31,
with the exact Kummer normalization of A.35. Their
modulo-three characters are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
       &m&n&t\\\hline
 \kappa_\zeta&1&0&0\\
 \kappa_{17}&0&0&1
 \end{array}.
 \tag{A.37.4}
\]
The restriction map to (A.37.2), composed with the
actual free pro-three presentation, is a continuous
epimorphism
\[
 F_3(m,n,t)\longrightarrow
 G_{K_0,\{3,17\}}(3)\longrightarrow G.
 \tag{A.37.5}
\]
Let $W\in D_3(F_3(m,n,t))$ be the actual arithmetic
Frobenius word of A.30. Under (A.37.5),
\[
 W\longmapsto\tau_{(2,2,2)},\qquad
 [t,[t,m]]\longmapsto\tau_{(1,1,1)}.
 \tag{A.37.6}
\]
In the restricted degree-three Lie algebra
$D_3(F_3)/D_4(F_3)$, this map annihilates the three
generator cubes and every ordinary degree-three
component except the multidegree $(1,0,2)$ component
generated by $[t,[t,m]]$. Consequently the coefficient
of this bracket in the full $W$ is exactly $2\in\mathbb F_3$.
This records a coefficient involving tame inertia;
the map killing $t$ in A.31 does not retain it.
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison:
\S51.16, folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178,
formulas (371)--(379); Tasks A.6 and B.4.}

statement:
An actual Frobenius basis with completely specified finite class-two action. Let $F_2=\langle x,y\rangle$ be the geometric pro-three group of
$\mathbb P^1-\{0,1,\infty\}$, based at the unit tangent at zero,
and let
\[
 N=\ker(F_2\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/3)^2),\qquad
 K=N^3\gamma_3N.
 \tag{A.38.1}
\]
Here $N^3$ is the closed subgroup generated by cubes. There is
an actual Frobenius $u$ at the prime $(7,\zeta-2)$ of $K_0$ such
that $u,v=cuc$ are a free basis of $P_3$, their integral action
on $V$ is exactly A.7, and their action on $N/K$ is the following
fully specified finite action. Complex conjugation is induced by
$x\mapsto x^{-1},y\mapsto y^{-1}$. The restriction of Frobenius
$u$ to $N/K$ equals the restriction of the following
automorphism of $F_2/K$:
\[
 x\longmapsto x^7,\qquad y\longmapsto f_0^{-1}y^7f_0.
 \tag{A.38.2}
\]
In the ordered Schreier basis
\[
\begin{split}
 &(yxy^{-1}x^{-1},\ y^2xy^{-2}x^{-1},\ y^3,\
 xyxy^{-1}x^{-2},\ xy^2xy^{-2}x^{-2},\ xy^3x^{-1},\\
 &\hspace{25mm}x^3,\ x^2yxy^{-1},\ x^2y^2xy^{-2},\
 x^2y^3x^{-2}),
\end{split}
 \tag{A.38.3}
\]
write $N/K$ as $\mathbb F_3^{10}\oplus\bigwedge^2\mathbb F_3^{10}$
with product $(a,z)(b,w)=(a+b,z+w+\tfrac12a\wedge b)$.
The word-class representative $f_0$ defining this finite
automorphism has coordinates
\[
 a_f=(0,0,1,1,2,0,2,0,1,2),
 \tag{A.38.4}
\]
and, in lexicographic order $i<j$, the forty-five central
coordinates are
\[
\begin{split}
 z_f={}&(2,1,2,1,1,2,0,1,2,\ 1,1,0,0,0,2,2,0,1,\\
       &1,1,1,1,1,0,1,1,0,0,1,2,0,0,1,0,1,1,\\
       &0,0,1,2,0,2,2,0,0).
\end{split}
 \tag{A.38.5}
\]
Thus (A.38.2)--(A.38.5) specify every coordinate of the images
of the ten geometric generators. They specify a representative
for the induced finite action; the actual Ihara word can differ
by the kernel of its map to that action. The arithmetic basis
is obtained from any initial
Frobenius basis by at most four explicitly described conjugations
below. The underlying Galois action and tangential origin are
retained; all cocycles and all arithmetic Frobenius words are
transported by the resulting actual source automorphism.

statement:
Global exclusions at seventeen inside the exact local cusp packet. Use the actual arithmetic basis of A.38, with $m,n$ and the
normalized local Frobenius $\varphi=\varphi_{17}$ transported
as there. Put $M_2=\bigwedge^2V$ and define the integral
normalized cochain module and its actual evaluation map by
\[
\begin{split}
 D&=M_2^{c=1}\oplus M_2^{nc=-1},\\
 E_\varphi:D&\longrightarrow M_2^{c=1},\quad
       (a,b)\longmapsto\gamma_{a,b}(\varphi),\\
 R&=\ker E_\varphi.
\end{split}
 \tag{A.39.1}
\]
Here $\gamma_{a,b}$ is the unique continuous cocycle on
$P_3\rtimes\langle c\rangle$ with values $(a,b,0)$ at
$(m,n,c)$. The lattice $D$ has rank $45$, and $R$ is a
saturated lattice of rank $24$.

For $r\in R$, twist the class-two image of the global
$O$-cuspidal section with tangent parameter $17$ by
$\gamma_r$. This defines an injectively parameterized family
of global class-two section classes, unramified outside
$\{3,17,\infty\}$. Every member has the same exact local
$O$-cusp section at seventeen, including its Frobenius
coordinate, and every member has a global class-three lift.

There is an $\mathbb F_3$-linear obstruction on $R/3R$ of
rank at least three which vanishes on every member lifting to
any of
\[
 N,\qquad N/N'',\qquad N/\gamma_3(I_{Q_c}).
 \tag{A.39.2}
\]
Consequently, from any integral basis $r_1,\ldots,r_{24}$ of
the kernel in (A.39.1), at least three of the resulting
twenty-four class-two section classes have none of the lifts
in (A.39.2). This is an unconditional finite-family existence
certificate. It does not select an unevaluated individual
basis vector as a counterexample. No assertion of full local
liftability at three is included.
An individually specified member of $R$ with nonzero
obstruction, including all integral generator coordinates
and a nine-term detecting functional, is given in B.20.

statement:
The exact completed Fox image and fibers on the cusp family. For the family $R$ in A.39 put
\[
 Q=N/N'',\qquad M=N'/N'',\qquad
 \Lambda=\mathbb Z_3[[V]],\qquad
 \mathfrak a=\ker(\Lambda\to\mathbb Z_3),\qquad J=\mathfrak aM.
 \tag{A.41.1}
\]
Give $M$ the arithmetic action twisted by the actual reference
$O$ section with tangent parameter $17$. Thus $m,n,c$ have
their original actions, and tame inertia acts by conjugation
by $c_O$. Define
\[
\begin{split}
 D_M&=M^{c=1}\oplus M^{nc=-1},\qquad
 D_J=J^{c=1}\oplus J^{nc=-1},\\
 E_W:D_M&\longrightarrow M^{c=1},\qquad
 E_W(a,b)=\beta_{a,b}(W),
\end{split}
 \tag{A.41.2}
\]
where $\beta_{a,b}$ is the continuous crossed cochain on the
free arithmetic source with values $(a,b,0,0)$ at
$(m,n,t,c)$. These are continuous linear maps of compact
$\mathbb Z_3$-modules. The natural quotient $M\to M_2$ gives
$\pi:D_M\twoheadrightarrow D$, with kernel $D_J$, and the
complete metabelian image on this family is exactly
\[
                  R_{\rm met}=\pi(\ker E_W)\subset R.
 \tag{A.41.3}
\]
Equivalently, it is the kernel of the explicit continuous map
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathfrak o_M:R&\longrightarrow
                   J^{c=1}/E_W(D_J),\\
 r&\longmapsto[\,E_W(\widetilde r)\,],
\end{split}
 \tag{A.41.4}
\]
where $\pi(\widetilde r)=r$. Every nonempty fiber of
$\operatorname{Sec}(Q)\to\operatorname{Sec}(N/\gamma_3N)$
over this family is an affine copy of
\[
             \ker(E_W:D_J\longrightarrow J^{c=1}).
 \tag{A.41.5}
\]
There is no remaining conjugacy quotient after the actual
local normalization in the proof. Formulas (A.41.2)--(A.41.5)
retain the completed arithmetic Fox operator. They do not
assign a numerical value to an unevaluated coefficient of
$W$ or of its action.

statement:
A complete affine Fox criterion for every one-prime inert metabelian target. Let $q\ne3$ be inert in $K_0$, and let $s$ be any class-two
section unramified outside $\{3,q,\infty\}$. Use the actual
presentation of A.28, written in the free basis $m,n,t$ with
$c(m)=m$, $c(n)=n^{-1}$, $c(t)=t^{-1}$, and put $Q_q=q^2$.
Retain its actual $c$-fixed Frobenius word $W$. Normalize
$s(c)=1$, and choose an equivariant lift $\widetilde s$ of
its three generator values to $Q=N/N''$ on this free source.
Such a lift always exists before imposing the single relator.

Let $\rho_\alpha$ be the action on $J=\gamma_3N/N''$ obtained
by conjugation by $\widetilde s$, where $\alpha$ is the
prescribed abelian section. Set
\[
 U=\rho_\alpha(m),\quad B=\rho_\alpha(n),\quad
 T=\rho_\alpha(t),\quad C=\rho_\alpha(c),\quad
 \Phi=\rho_\alpha(W).
 \tag{A.42.1}
\]
This action depends only on $\alpha$ and descends to the
actual arithmetic group. In particular
$\Phi T\Phi^{-1}=T^{Q_q}$. Define
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal D_\alpha&=
 J^{C=1}\oplus J^{BC=-1}\oplus J^{TC=-1},\\
 \mathcal J_\alpha&=J^{T^{Q_q}C=-1},\\
 \mathcal E_W(a,b,d)&=
 \rho_\alpha\!\left(\frac{\partial W}{\partial m}\right)a+
 \rho_\alpha\!\left(\frac{\partial W}{\partial n}\right)b+
 \rho_\alpha\!\left(\frac{\partial W}{\partial t}\right)d,\\
 \mathcal L_s(a,b,d)&=(1-T^{Q_q})\mathcal E_W(a,b,d)
                +\left(\Phi-\sum_{i=0}^{Q_q-1}T^i\right)d,\\
 e_s&=\widetilde s(WtW^{-1}t^{-Q_q})\in\mathcal J_\alpha.
\end{split}
 \tag{A.42.2}
\]
The full global metabelian image consists exactly of the
targets for which
\[
             [e_s]=0\quad\text{in}\quad
                  \mathcal J_\alpha/\mathcal L_s(\mathcal D_\alpha).
 \tag{A.42.3}
\]
For every target in that image, its fiber is an affine torsor
under the explicitly specified compact group
\[
 \frac{\ker\mathcal L_s}
 {\{((U-1)h,(B-1)h,(T-1)h):h\in J^{C=1}\}}.
 \tag{A.42.4}
\]
All source actions, the affine error, and the finite images of
$W$ in these formulas are the actual based ones. The criterion
is an exact completed linear system, including its affine
origin and every conjugation. Its numerical evaluation for
arbitrary input is not asserted.

statement:
Finite arithmetic image and fiber tests with arbitrary ramification support. Let $s$ be an exact continuous class-two section, normalized
by $s(c)=1$, and let $\alpha$ be its abelian projection.
The following construction applies to each of
\[
       G=N,\qquad G=N/N'',\qquad G=N/\gamma_3(I_{Q_c}).
 \tag{A.43.1}
\]
It gives an exact image criterion and every fiber using
explicit finite arithmetic fields, finite groups, and finite
cocycle sets. The target may have infinite ramification
support.

Put $H_0=N$, $H_{n+1}=\Phi(H_n)=H_n^3[H_n,H_n]$, with
closures understood. The finite tests below are indexed by
$n\ge1$; set
\[
\begin{split}
 P_n&=N/H_n,\qquad A_n=N/(H_n\gamma_3N),\\
 G_n&=P_n,\quad P_n/P_n'',\quad
                 P_n/\gamma_3(I_n),
\end{split}
 \tag{A.43.2}
\]
in the three cases, where $I_n$ is the normal closure of
the actual image of $c_{Q_c}$ in $P_n$. Write $s_n$ for the
exact target cocycle in $A_n$, and let
\[
 S_n=\{3,\infty\}\cup
       \{q\ne3:\alpha\bmod3^n\text{ is ramified at }q\}.
 \tag{A.43.3}
\]
These are explicitly determined finite increasing sets at
each precision. All finite geometric groups and their based
arithmetic actions are constructed by the iterated elementary
abelian covers in the proof.

Let $F_n$ be the finite Galois field splitting the action on
$G_n$. Let $K_n$ be its compositum with the finite Galois
field cut out by the target homomorphism
$g\mapsto(s_n(g),\rho_{A_n}(g))$. If $s_n$ is ramified
outside $S_n$, the solution set below is empty immediately.
Otherwise put
\[
 d_n=|G_n|[F_n:\mathbb Q],\qquad
 B_n=\prod_{p\in S_n\setminus\{\infty\}}
               p^{d_n(1+\lfloor\log_p d_n\rfloor)}.
 \tag{A.43.4}
\]
Set $\Omega_0=\mathbb Q$. Construct $\Omega_n$ as the compositum of $\Omega_{n-1}$
and all Galois extensions $E/\mathbb Q$ containing $K_n$,
unramified outside $S_n$, and of degree at most $d_n$.
The degree and discriminant bound $B_n$ make this a
terminating finite field enumeration. Put
$\Delta_n=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega_n/\mathbb Q)$.

Define $X_n(s,G)$ by finite enumeration of all functions
$z:\Delta_n\to G_n$ satisfying
\[
\begin{split}
 z(gh)&=z(g)\,g(z(h)),\qquad z(c)=1,\\
 \pi_n z&=s_n,
\end{split}
 \tag{A.43.5}
\]
and the following finite additional conditions: for every
$k\le n$, its projection to $G_k$ is trivial on the inertia
groups at every prime of $S_n\setminus S_k$. The target and
coefficient actions in (A.43.5) are inflated through their
specified finite fields. A failed immediate test makes all
subsequent solution sets empty.

There are explicitly induced transition maps between these
finite sets, and
\[
 [s]\in\operatorname{im}
    \bigl(\operatorname{Sec}(G)\to\operatorname{Sec}(N/\gamma_3N)\bigr)
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                 X_n(s,G)\ne\varnothing\text{ for every }n.
 \tag{A.43.6}
\]
Let $J_n=\ker(G_n\to A_n)$, with its actual $c$-action.
The entire fiber over $[s]$ is
\[
                      \varprojlim_n\bigl(X_n(s,G)/J_n^c\bigr),
 \tag{A.43.7}
\]
where $h\in J_n^c$ acts by
$z(g)\mapsto h^{-1}z(g)g(h)$. Thus the finite quotients in
the fiber use the kernels $J_n$, with no replacement by a
finite-level centralizer of the target.

Each stage is a terminating arithmetic construction from
the finite target data at that precision. Formula (A.43.6)
is an infinite sequence of finite tests; no finite stopping
rule for every positive instance is asserted.

statement:
Inherited comparison and every marked coefficient layer. Let $F$ be the free pro-three geometric group of
$\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, with the based
generators $x,y$ of A.38. The actual Fermat covering and
its specified tangential comparison identify
\[
 N=\ker\bigl(F\longrightarrow(\mathbb Z/3)^2\bigr),
 \qquad c_{Q_c}=y^3.
 \tag{A.44.1}
\]
Put $J_y=\overline{\langle\!\langle y\rangle\!\rangle}_F$
and $I=I_{Q_c}$. The inherited quotients and their actual
comparison maps are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 N/N''&\twoheadrightarrow H_{\rm met}
       :=\operatorname{im}(N\to F/F''),\\
 &\ker=(N\cap F'')/N'',\\
 N/\gamma_3I&\twoheadrightarrow H_{\rm depth}
       :=\operatorname{im}(N\to F/\gamma_3J_y),\\
 &\ker=(N\cap\gamma_3J_y)/\gamma_3I.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{A.44.2}
\]
These are continuous genuine $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant
surjections, with the origins of A.38. The second is
precisely the pro-three instance of LM7 (E25.1).
At the prounipotent level over $\mathbb Q_3$ the image in each
specified quotient of the base group is the whole base
quotient. On abelian Lie algebras the map from the
intrinsic group has kernel of dimension eight.

Set $Q=N/\gamma_3I$ and
$M_r^{\rm mark}=\gamma_rQ/\gamma_{r+1}Q$.
There is an actual quotient of graded $\mathbb Z_3$-Lie
algebras
\[
 \operatorname{gr}_{\gamma}Q
   =\mathcal L(V)/\gamma_3\mathfrak j,
 \qquad \mathfrak j=(e_{Q_c})_{\mathcal L(V)}.
 \tag{A.44.3}
\]
Every graded piece is finite free. Choose the free factor
$B$ of rank nine obtained by omitting the generator
$y^3$ from the ten literal Schreier generators of A.38,
and put $V_B=B^{\rm ab}$. As a choice of integral bases,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 M_r^{\rm mark}\simeq{}&
 \mathcal L_r(V_B)\ \oplus\
 V_B^{\otimes(r-1)}e_{Q_c}\\
 &{}\oplus\left(\bigwedge\nolimits^2
       \bigl(\mathrm T(V_B)e_{Q_c}\bigr)\right)_r.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{A.44.4}
\]
Here a tensor word of length $a$ followed by $e_{Q_c}$
has ordinary degree $a+1$. The arithmetic action is the
one induced by (A.44.3) from the actual action on $V$;
(A.44.4) does not impose a block diagonal arithmetic
action. For $r\ge2$ its rank is
\[
 \frac1r\sum_{d\mid r}\mu(d)9^{r/d}
 +9^{r-1}
 +\frac{(r-1)9^{r-2}
          -\mathbf1_{2\mid r}\,9^{r/2-1}}2.
 \tag{A.44.5}
\]
In particular the ranks in degrees one through four are
$10,45,330,2466$.

For $r\ge3$, put $A_{r,q}=M_r^{\rm mark}(-1)$ and
$D_{r,q}=\operatorname{Frob}_q-1$ on that lattice.
Every $D_{r,q}$ is injective, and, with the restricted
families of F.1, the complete coefficient formulas are
\[
\begin{split}
 H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},M_r^{\rm mark})
    &=\mathcal R(A_r)/D_r\mathcal R(A_r),\\
 \varprojlim{}^1_n H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},M_r^{\rm mark}/3^n)
    &=\frac{\mathcal R(A_r)\cap
                   \prod_{q\ne3}D_{r,q}A_{r,q}}
                 {D_r\mathcal R(A_r)}\ne0,\\
 H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},M_r^{\rm mark})
    &=M_r^{\rm mark}/(u-1)(M_r^{\rm mark})^c.
\end{split}
 \tag{A.44.6}
\]
The quotient functor (A.44.3), applied to the matrices
of A.7, gives all action matrices and hence an integral
Smith calculation of the last group at every degree.
Degrees one and two are $V$ and $\bigwedge^2V$; their
derived limits are those of F.5 and are also nonzero.
Together with A.21--A.22, these formulas specify the
cofinal finite-rank towers and the derived-limit term
of every layer required in Task A.6. Their exact images
and all fibers are the finite arithmetic sets of A.43.

statement:
The three abelian cusp packets, with their framed origins. Put $J=J_{E,D}$ and use the frame coordinates of LM7 (E24.4).
Let $z_P$ be the framed line bundle $\mathcal O(P-O)$ with frames
$(x/z)^{-1}$ at $P$, $z/x$ at $O$, and the canonical section at the
other cusps.  Define $z_Q$ in the same way from $Q_c-O$, using $y/z$
at $Q_c$.  Put $\alpha_P=\kappa(z_P)$, $\alpha_Q=\kappa(z_Q)$ and
$\alpha_O=0$.  The three packets in $H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},V)$ are
\[
 \mathscr P_d^V=\alpha_d+e_d\,\mathcal R_{\mathbb P}(\mathbb Z_3),
 \qquad d=O,P,Q_c.                                      \tag{B.1}
\]
Here $e_d\,\mathcal R_{\mathbb P}(\mathbb Z_3)$ denotes the image of
the continuous homomorphism on cohomology induced by the
$G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant inclusion
$\mathbb Z_3(1)\to V$, $1\mapsto e_d$.

The torus-point relation specifying the second framed origin is
\[
 z_P+z_Q=
 (3^{-1},3^{-1},-\lambda^{-1},-\lambda^{-1},\zeta\lambda^{-2}).
                                                               \tag{B.2}
\]
In the presentation (E24.7), eliminate the first $\lambda$-generator
and retain $z'$.  Write $g_2,g_3$ for the remaining two
$\lambda$-generators and $\tau_3$ for $\zeta$ in the third quadratic
factor.  After pro-$3$ completion the origins have toric coordinates
zero, divisible-cohomology coordinate zero, and remaining coordinates
\[
 \alpha_P=\kappa(z'),\qquad
 \alpha_Q=\kappa(2z'+g_2+g_3-\tau_3).                   \tag{B.3}
\]
The inertia maps in the original frame coordinates are
\[
 \begin{split}
 i_O(u)&=(u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-1},u^{-1}),\\
 i_P(u)&=(u,1,1,1,1),\qquad i_Q(u)=(1,u,1,1,1).
 \end{split}                                               \tag{B.4}
\]
Their images under the two coordinate-unit characters are respectively
$(-\kappa u,-\kappa u)$, $(\kappa u,0)$ and $(0,\kappa u)$.
The three sets in (B.1) are pairwise disjoint, and each displayed
parameter map is injective.

statement:
The inherited class-two image need not be a point or cusp image. The exclusion proposed in Lead 1 is false.  There are sections of
$N\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$ whose image in $\operatorname{Sec}(H)$
has toric coordinates $(\kappa(3),2\kappa(3))$.  Every such image
lies outside the three rational cusp packets, and $U(\mathbb Q)$
has no point producing it.  It therefore supplies the asserted
counterexample already with a full geometric pro-$3$ lift.

statement:
The cusp packets in the cuspidally central quotient. In $N^{\rm cc}=C\times_TV$, let the generator of the central
$\mathbb Z_3(1)$ of $C$ be the elliptic commutator $[a,b]$.
Choose the reference $C$-section above the elliptic class zero
to be the tangent at $O$; above $\kappa(P-O)$ and
$\kappa(Q_c-O)$ choose the images of the respective unit tangents.
Use these references for every abelian class in the corresponding
three elliptic fibers.  With these explicit choices for the
torsors denoted by $s(\alpha,a)$, the cusp packets are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
 d&\alpha&a\\ \hline
 O&e_O\kappa(u)&-\kappa(u)\\
 P&\alpha_P+e_P\kappa(u)&0\\
 Q_c&\alpha_Q+e_{Q_c}\kappa(u)&0
 \end{array}                                                \tag{B.6}
\]
Here $u$ ranges over the full pro-$3$ completion of
$\mathbb Q^\times$.  This parametrization is injective on each
row, and the rows have disjoint images.

statement:
Lead 4 for the full geometric pro-three group. For every continuous section
$s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to N\rtimes G_{\mathbb Q}$ put
$\Delta=\ker(\chi:G_{\mathbb Q}\to\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times})$.
Then
\[
 C_N(s(\Delta))=
 \begin{cases}
 I_{\widetilde d},&s\text{ is cuspidal at the lifted cusp }\widetilde d,\\
 1,&s\text{ is noncuspidal}.
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{B.7}
\]
In the first case the lifted cusp is unique and its image is one
of $O,P,Q_c$.  Thus both implications in Lead 4 hold for the
actual pro-$3$ group, with its genuine section action.

statement:
The cuspidal members of the full unramified family. Let $\mathscr F_S$ be the image of
$H^1(G_{\mathbb Q,\{3,\infty\}},N)$ in
$H^1(G_{\mathbb Q},N)$, using the integral tangent at $O$.
Its cuspidal subset is the disjoint union of the three
packets obtained by twisting the unit tangents at
$O,P,Q_c$ by $t\kappa(3)$, $t\in\mathbb Z_3$.
Every other full section class in $\mathscr F_S$ has
centralizer $1$ over $\Delta$.  The centralizer of each
cuspidal member is its complete pro-$3$ inertia group.

statement:
The complete global one-prime image and its fibers. Fix a rational prime $q\ne3$, put
$A=N/\gamma_3N$, and let $s$ be a continuous
class-two section unramified outside
$S=\{3,q,\infty\}$. Choose its exact cocycle
representative with $s(c)=1$, and write $\alpha$
for its projection to $V$. Define
\[
 \begin{split}
 H_0&=N,\qquad H_{n+1}=H_n^3[H_n,H_n],\\
 P_n&=N/H_n,\qquad A_n=P_n/\gamma_3P_n,\qquad
 J_n=\gamma_3P_n,\\
 S_n&=\{3,\infty\}\cup
 \{q:\alpha|_{I_q}\bmod3^n\ne0\}.
 \end{split}                                               \tag{B.6.1}
\]
All subgroups are closed. The exact finite target
$s_n$ is the image of $s$ in $A_n$.

Use the explicitly constructed finite based action on
$P_n$ and its splitting field $F_n$ from A.43.
Let $K_n$ be the compositum of $F_n$ with the
field of the target graph $(s_n,\rho_{A_n})$.
If $s_n$ is ramified outside $S_n$, the test fails.
Otherwise form the finite Galois field $\Omega_n$
as the compositum of $\Omega_{n-1}$ and all Galois
extensions $E/\mathbb Q$ containing $K_n$,
unramified outside $S_n$, of degree at most
$|P_n|[F_n:\mathbb Q]$, starting with
$\Omega_0=\mathbb Q$.
The discriminant and polynomial bounds in
(A.43.4)--(A.43.10) give a terminating finite
enumeration of these fields.

Let $X_n$ be the finite set of functions
$z:\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega_n/\mathbb Q)\to P_n$
satisfying the actual cocycle equation,
$z(c)=1$, and $z\bmod J_n=s_n$ literally.
For every $k\le n$, require its projection to
$P_k$ to be trivial on inertia at the primes
of $S_n\setminus S_k$. These conditions give
the actual transition maps of A.43. Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 [s]\in\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Sec}(N)
          \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}(A)\bigr)
 &\Longleftrightarrow X_n\ne\varnothing\quad\text{for all }n\\
 &\Longleftrightarrow
 [s]\text{ lifts to }N/\gamma_rN
                    \quad\text{for all }r\ge3.
 \end{split}                                               \tag{B.6.2}
\]
Every such full or nilpotent lift is unramified
outside $S$. The complete fiber on section classes is
\[
                 \varprojlim_n X_n/J_n^c,                  \tag{B.6.3}
\]
where $h\in J_n^c$ acts by
$z(g)\mapsto h^{-1}z(g)g(h)$.
Thus (B.6.2) is an exact sequence of terminating
finite arithmetic tests, and (B.6.3) retains all
compatible conjugacy data. A bounded stopping rule
for every positive instance is not asserted.

The necessary local condition is precisely the
unramified class or a member of the actual cusp
packets (B.8.1). It is sufficient at seven by
B.10, and on the prime sets $\Sigma$ and $\Xi$
by A.16 and A.25. It is insufficient at seventeen.
The integral section of B.20, with abelian class
$\kappa(17)e_O$ and central generator values
$\gamma(m)=0$, $\gamma(n)=b$, has exactly the
local $O$-cuspidal class-two restriction. It has
a global $N/\gamma_4N$ lift and no
$N/\gamma_5N$ lift, hence no full, metabelian,
or marked-depth lift.

statement:
Every nontrivial tame inertia in a full section is cuspidal. Let $q\ne3$ be a rational prime, put $k=\mathbb Q_q$, and
use the actual pro-three fundamental group $N$ of the marked
Fermat cubic with the integral unit tangent at $O$ as origin.
For a continuous section $s:G_k\to N\rtimes G_k$, its
restriction to inertia is either trivial or has image in one
cuspidal inertia subgroup.  In the latter case the whole
section is contained in that cusp's decomposition group.
The cusp is $k$-rational and the lifted cusp is unique.
Moreover, a full section is unramified at $q$ exactly when
its image in $V$ is unramified there.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The exact local image of ramified full sections in class two. With $k=\mathbb Q_q$, $q\ne3$, let $A=N/\gamma_3N$.
For each $d\in D(k)$ choose the coordinate unit tangent
used in C.10, its actual section $s_{d,1}$, and a peripheral
generator $c_d$ based at $O$.  The ramified part of the image
of full sections in $\operatorname{Sec}_k(A)$ is precisely
the disjoint union
\[
 \coprod_{d\in D(k)}
 \left\{
  \left[g\longmapsto
    c_d^{\kappa_q(u)(g)}s_{d,1}(g)\right]:
  u\in k^{\times\wedge_3},\ v_q(u)\ne0
 \right\}.                                                   \tag{B.8.1}
\]
Here the expression is multiplication in the arithmetic
group, followed by its actual class-two quotient.
Its parameter space is explicitly
\[
 k^{\times\wedge_3}
   =\mathbb Z_3\kappa(q)\oplus\mu_{3^{v_3(q-1)}}(k).
                                                               \tag{B.8.2}
\]
There are nine packets for $q\equiv1\pmod3$ and three for
$q\equiv2\pmod3$.  In the central cuspidal lattice
$I/[N,I]=\mathbb Z_3(1)[D]$ the tame vector of a packet is
$v_q(u)c_d$, with exactly this one cusp coordinate nonzero.
In particular the mixed-inertia counterexamples in A.5 and
A.6 cannot lift to full $N$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
All inherited class-two cusp origins. Use exactly the diagonal coordinates of LM7 E.29 for $H$,
based at the lifted cusp $P$ over $t=0$, and put
\[
       f(g)=\frac{\chi_3(g)^2-1}{24}\in\mathbb Z_3(2).
                                                               \tag{B.9.1}
\]
The three rational cusp packets in $\operatorname{Sec}(H)$
have the following continuous cocycle representatives:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &u(g)&v(g)&w(g)\\ \hline
 P&\kappa(a)(g)&0&0\\
 Q_c&0&\kappa(a)(g)&f(g)\\
 O&-\kappa(a)(g)&-\kappa(a)(g)&f(g)/2
 \end{array}
 \qquad a\in\mathbb Q^{\times\wedge_3}.                    \tag{B.9.2}
\]
Each row is injectively parametrized and the rows are
pairwise disjoint.  Above inherited abelian class $(0,0)$
the three unit tangents give, respectively, the central
labels $0,2,1\in\mathbb Z/3$ relative to
$g\mapsto(\chi_3(g)^2-1)/3$.
The actual arithmetic map from the intrinsic group based
at $O$ to this $H$-extension is
\[
 (n,g)\longmapsto
    \bigl(q_O(n)(0,0,f(g)/2),g\bigr),                       \tag{B.9.3}
\]
after the geometric path choices in the proof.
Thus (B.9.2) retains the change of section origin between
the $O$ and $P$ base points.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The full global image at the specified prime seven. Let $A=N/\gamma_3N$, and use the normalized pair coordinates
$(a,b)$ and the $A^c$-action of A.15 for sections supported
at $\{3,7,\infty\}$.  Such a class has a full $N$-lift
exactly in the following cases:
\[
 b=1,
 \quad\text{or its restriction to }G_{\mathbb Q_7}
       \text{ belongs to one of the nine ramified packets (B.8.1).}
                                                               \tag{B.10.1}
\]
Equivalently these are precisely the classes which lift to
every lower-central quotient.  A full lift can be chosen
unramified outside $\{3,7,\infty\}$.

Here is an exact packet parametrization in the pair
coordinates.  Fix the embedding $\zeta_3\equiv2\pmod7$,
a Frobenius $\phi$ fixing compatible roots of $7$, and the
actual unit-tangent values $g_d=s_{d,1}(\phi)\in A$.
Use the same based inertia element $c_d\in A$ in each case.
The ramified part of the global image is
\[
 \left\{
  \bigl[(c_d^{2j}g_d,c_d^v)\cdot h\bigr]:
    d\in D(\mathbb Q_7),\quad
    v\in\mathbb Z_3\setminus\{0\},\quad j\in\{0,1,2\},
    \quad h\in A/A^c
 \right\}.                                                   \tag{B.10.2}
\]
Here $(a,b)\cdot h=(h^{-1}aF(h),h^{-1}bh)$, so $A/A^c$
means right cosets, and the displayed parameters are
injective after these explicit choices.  The symbols
$g_d$ retain the actual tangential Frobenius origins;
they are not replaced by arbitrary solutions of a
graded normalization equation.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
No new ramification above class two and compactness for a finite set of primes. Let $S$ be any finite set of rational places containing
$3$ and infinity, and let $s_2$ be a class-two section
unramified outside $S$.  Every lift of $s_2$ to
$N/\gamma_rN$, $r\ge3$, is unramified outside the same
set $S$.  Moreover the following assertions are equivalent:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 s_2\text{ lifts to }N;\\
 s_2\text{ lifts to }N/\gamma_rN\text{ for every }r\ge3.
 \end{gathered}                                               \tag{B.11.1}
\]
The separately given nilpotent lifts need not be
compatible.  The conclusion supplies a compatible
continuous full lift, also unramified outside $S$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The marked local classification when the filled-curve projection is unramified. Let $k/\mathbb Q_q$ be finite, $q\ne3$, with residue cardinality
$Q$, and let $d=Q_c$ be the marked cusp. Write
\[
 \mathscr Q=N/\gamma_3I_{\rm mark},\qquad
 B=N/I_{\rm mark},\qquad
 \mathscr I=I_{\rm mark}/\gamma_3I_{\rm mark},\qquad
 Z=\gamma_2I_{\rm mark}/\gamma_3I_{\rm mark}.
 \tag{B.12.1}
\]
All groups carry the actual arithmetic action, and the
quotient $B$ is the full geometric pro-three group of the
curve obtained by filling $d$.
Choose tame three-inertia $\tau$, arithmetic Frobenius
$\phi$, the peripheral generator $c$ at $d$, and the
unit tangential reference $s_{d,1}$ compatibly.
Put $F_0=s_{d,1}(\phi)$.
The induced based action $\Phi$ of $F_0$ on $B$ is
the action of the point $d$ on the filled curve.
There are actual equivariant identifications
\[
 M:=\mathscr I^{\rm ab}
     =\mathbb Z_3[[B]](1),\qquad
 Z=\widehat{\bigwedge}^{\,2}M,\qquad
 (F_0)_M=Q\Phi,\quad (F_0)_Z=Q^2\widehat{\bigwedge}^{\,2}\Phi.
 \tag{B.12.2}
\]
Here the completed modules are inverse limits over finite
continuous partitions of the profinite label set $B$;
the label $1$ is the chosen lift of the marked cusp.

Every local section of $\mathscr Q$ whose projection to $B$
is unramified and whose tame inertia is nontrivial has,
up to geometric conjugation, exactly the following form:
\[
 s(\tau)=c^a,\qquad s(\phi)=c^r\exp(z)F_0,
 \quad
 \begin{cases}
 a\in\mathbb Z_3\setminus\{0\},\\
 r\in\mathbb Z_3/(Q-1)\mathbb Z_3,\\
 [z]\in\mathcal C_{k,d}:=
 Z/(Q^2\widehat{\bigwedge}^{\,2}\Phi-1)Z .
 \end{cases}                                                \tag{B.12.3}
\]
In particular its $B$-section is the point section at $d$.
The quotient in (B.12.3) uses the actual image; that image
is closed because $Z$ is compact.
Every displayed parameter occurs, and two displayed
sections are conjugate exactly when all three parameters
agree.

Under $\mathscr Q\to N/\gamma_3N$, their image is exactly
the ramified local cusp packet at $d$. For each member of
that packet the entire local fiber is the group
$\mathcal C_{k,d}$, acting simply transitively after the
displayed reference is fixed.
Finally a local marked section whose abelian tame inertia
in $V$ is zero is itself unramified.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The central marked local fiber is a countable product of three-adic integers. The group $\mathcal C_{k,d}$ in (B.12.3) is a nonzero,
torsion-free, compact metrizable $\mathbb Z_3$-module.
After a choice of divisible basis of its discrete dual,
there is a continuous $\mathbb Z_3$-linear isomorphism
\[
                         \mathcal C_{k,d}
                                  \simeq\prod_{n\ge1}\mathbb Z_3 .
                                                               \tag{B.13.1}
\]
The coordinates in (B.13.1) depend on that stated choice;
the quotient and the section action in (B.12.3) are
intrinsic to the displayed reference.
In particular there are actual local marked sections
with the same ramified class-two cusp image which
are not cuspidal and have no full-$N$ lift.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The complete local marked image and the unmarked ramified fibers. Retain the local data and actual quotients of B.12.
If the projection of a section of $\mathscr Q$ to $B$
is ramified, that section is itself cuspidal at a
unique unmarked cusp $d'\in D(k)\setminus\{d\}$.
For a fixed ramified $B$-section the lift to
$\mathscr Q$, up to geometric conjugation, is unique
and is the image of its actual full cusp section.

Consequently the complete local image of
$\operatorname{Sec}_k(\mathscr Q)$ in
$\operatorname{Sec}_k(N/\gamma_3N)$ equals the
local full image: all unramified classes and the
disjoint ramified cusp packets of B.8.
The fiber over a ramified unmarked cusp class is
a singleton; the fiber over a ramified marked
cusp class is exactly the group $\mathcal C_{k,d}$
of B.12--B.13.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
An explicit cleaned Heisenberg detector at seven. Put $k=\mathbb F_7(\theta)$, $\theta^3=2$, and write
$[a,b,c]=a+b\theta+c\theta^2$.  On
$E_k:y^2+y=x^3$, let $\zeta=2$ and
\[
 \begin{split}
 P&=(3,2),\qquad P^-=(3,4),\\
 Q&=([4,1,1],[2,0,2]),\\
 S&=([0,6,5],[1,4,3]),\\
 T_1&=([3,3,3],[6,2,2]),\qquad T_2=-T_1 .
 \end{split}                                               \tag{B.15.1}
\]
The following functions are explicit:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 a&=\frac{x^2+[1,6,5]x+[0,1,4]+[4,4,4]y}{x-3},&
 b&=x-3,\\
 f_1&=\frac{x^2+[2,3,5]x+[6,4,6]+[6,1,6]y}
                  {x-[3,3,3]},\\
 f_2&=\frac{x^2+[2,3,5]x+[0,3,0]+[1,6,1]y}
                  {x-[3,3,3]},\\
 m&=\frac{x^2+[2,5,2]x+[6,2,2]+[2,4,5]y}
                  {x-[3,3,3]},&
 f&=\frac{m}{f_1f_2^2(x-[3,3,3])}.
 \end{aligned}                                             \tag{B.15.2}
\]
Define $p(v)=\sum_{i=0}^5p_iv^i$ and
$h(v)=\sum_{i=0}^3h_iv^i$ by
\[
 \begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}
 i&0&1&2&3&4&5\\ \hline
 p_i&[3,0,0]&[0,6,6]&[6,1,5]&[4,0,2]&[4,1,2]&[1,5,4]\\
 h_i&[6,1,4]&[6,0,1]&[2,0,0]&[1,5,4]&&
 \end{array}                                               \tag{B.15.3}
\]
In $k(E)(v)$ with $v^3=b$, put
\[
 u(v)=\frac{p(v)+y}{v h(v)},\qquad
 r=f\,u(v)u(\zeta v)^2.                                    \tag{B.15.4}
\]
Then
\[
              v^3=b,\qquad w^3=a,\qquad z^3=r               \tag{B.15.5}
\]
defines a connected Galois cover of degree $27$, with
Heisenberg group of exponent three.  It is finite \'etale
over $U_k=E_k\setminus E_k[3]$.
The actual deck generators are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
       &v&w&z\\ \hline
 \sigma&\zeta v&w&u(\zeta^2v)z/w\\
 \tau&v&\zeta w&z\\
 \rho&v&w&\zeta z ,
 \end{array}
 \qquad [\sigma,\tau]=\rho.                                 \tag{B.15.6}
\]
For the Fermat tangent parameter $s$ at $O$, the first
two radicals retain the leading coefficient $9$, whose
reduction is $2$.  The cleaned central radical satisfies
$r\sim s^4$.  Thus the based Puiseux choices are
\[
 v\sim\theta s^{-2/3},\qquad
 w\sim\theta s^{-2/3},\qquad
 z\sim s^{4/3}.                                            \tag{B.15.7}
\]
There is also an explicit Frobenius transport on the
compositum of the three coefficient-conjugate covers.
Let a superscript $[j]$ mean raising every coefficient
to $7^j$, with $j$ read modulo three, and use the same
choices (B.15.7) for $w_j,z_j$.  The arithmetic
Frobenius at the framed tangent is
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Phi(v)&=\zeta^2v,\qquad
 \Phi(w_j)=\zeta^2w_{j+1},\\
 \Phi(z_j)&=
       \frac{\zeta w_{j+1}z_{j+1}}
                    {u^{[j+1]}(\zeta v)},\qquad
 \Phi^3=1 .
 \end{split}                                               \tag{B.15.15}
\]
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The integral depth-one map through the cyclic-nine cover. Let $F$ be the free pro-three group on the standard
tripod inertia generators $x,y$, with
$[x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$.
For $f\in F'$ write its metabelian image as
$[x,y]^{h(X,Y)}$, where $X=x-1$, $Y=y-1$ act by
conjugation.  There is an actual continuous
metabelian quotient in which
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 x\longmapsto(1,0),\qquad y\longmapsto(0,1),\\
 (m,a)(n,b)=(m+t^a n,a+b),\\
 m,n\in\mathbb Z_3[[t-1]],\qquad a,b\in\mathbb Z_3.
 \end{gathered}
                                                               \tag{B.16.1}
\]
In this quotient the image of $f$ is $(m_f,0)$, with
\[
                   m_f(t)=(1-t)h(0,t-1).                  \tag{B.16.2}
\]

Let $H_9=\ker(F\to\mathbb Z/9)$, where $x\mapsto0$,
$y\mapsto1$.  Its actual cover is
\[
 z^9=1-t_{\rm base},\qquad
 Y_9=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,\infty,\mu_9\}.
                                                               \tag{B.16.3}
\]
In $H_9^{\rm ab}/3$, write the image of $f$ as
$\sum_{j=0}^8c_j\,y^jxy^{-j}$; its $y^9$ coordinate
is zero.  Then
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}h_{0,3}\\h_{0,5}\end{pmatrix}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}
 0&0&0&0&2&1&0&1&2\\
 0&0&0&0&0&0&2&2&2
 \end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}c_0\\c_1\\c_2\\c_3\\c_4\\c_5\\c_6\\c_7\\c_8\end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{in }\mathbb F_3.                              \tag{B.16.4}
\]

For the standard path $\beta$ from $\overrightarrow{01}$
to $\overrightarrow{10}$ and the convention
$f_g=\beta(g\beta)^{-1}$, these coordinates are explicit
framed Kummer coordinates on (B.16.3).
The relevant endpoint-to-start ratios are
\[
 r_0=9,\qquad r_j=\frac{-\zeta_9^j}{1-\zeta_9^j}
       \quad(1\leq j\leq8),\qquad \prod_{j=0}^8r_j=1.
                                                               \tag{B.16.5}
\]
Choose their compatible roots by continuing the units
$z-\zeta_9^j$ along the lifted path from $z=1$ to $z=0$,
using the actual start velocity $-1/9$ for $j=0$.
If
\[
 \frac{g(r_{\chi(g)^{-1}j}^{\,1/3^n})}
      {r_j^{\,1/3^n}}
     =\zeta_{3^n}^{\,\kappa_j(g)},                          \tag{B.16.6}
\]
where the index is taken modulo nine, then
$c_j=-\kappa_j(g)\pmod3$.
In particular (B.16.4)--(B.16.6) evaluate the two
coefficients by finite cyclic-cover Kummer data for
the full cyclotomic action; no restriction to
$\ker\chi$ is imposed.

statement:
The actual norm-289 depth-one Frobenius coordinates. Let $g_{17}$ be an arithmetic Frobenius of norm $289$
at the prime above seventeen of $K_0=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3)$,
viewed through the specified tangential arithmetic action.
Use the path and commutator conventions of B.16, and write
the metabelian Ihara word as
$f_{g_{17}}=[x,y]^{h(X,Y)}$.
Then
\[
 h(0,Y)\equiv-Y^6-Y^7\pmod{(3,Y^8)},
 \qquad h_{0,3}=h_{0,5}=0\quad\text{in }\mathbb F_3.
                                                               \tag{B.17.1}
\]
An explicit residue-field embedding is
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 k=\mathbb F_{17}[\theta]/(\theta^2-3),\\
 \overline\zeta_9=7+4\theta,\qquad
 \overline\zeta_3=\overline\zeta_9^3=8+15\theta.
 \end{gathered}
                                                               \tag{B.17.2}
\]
For the nine framed ratios of B.16 the actual local
Kummer coordinates and geometric cusp coordinates are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 (\kappa_j(g_{17}))_{j=0}^8
       &=(0,1,2,0,1,2,0,1,2),\\
 (c_j)_{j=0}^8&=(0,2,1,0,2,1,0,2,1).
 \end{aligned}
                                                               \tag{B.17.3}
\]
The entries are in $\mathbb F_3$. These values hold for
each prime of $\mathbb Q(\zeta_9)$ above seventeen,
with its compatible embedding of $\zeta_3=\zeta_9^3$.

statement:
The full finite arithmetic image and the exact Frobenius action at seventeen. Use the actual source basis of A.38 and the
$c$-adapted basis $m,n$ of A.31. Let
\[
 \rho:P_3\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Aut}\bigl(N/(N^3\gamma_3N)\bigr)
\]
be the actual arithmetic action. Its image $G$
has order $243$, nilpotency class three, and
exponent nine. In the $10+45$ coordinates of A.38,
its linear image has order nine, and its
identity-linear kernel has dimension three over
$\mathbb F_3$. The exact dimensions are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
   &\gamma_2(G)&\gamma_3(G)&\gamma_4(G)\\\hline
 \dim_{\mathbb F_3}&2&1&0
 \end{array}
 \qquad
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
   &D_2(G)&D_3(G)&D_4(G)\\\hline
 \dim_{\mathbb F_3}&3&2&0.
 \end{array}
                                                               \tag{B.18.1}
\]
In particular $D_4(P_3)$ acts trivially on this
specified geometric quotient. Put
$M=\rho(m)$ and $N_*=\rho(n)$. Then the entire
actual Frobenius action at seventeen is
\[
 \rho(\varphi_{17})
   =M^6[N_*,[N_*,M]]=M^6\ne1.
                                                               \tag{B.18.2}
\]
It has order three. Its Johnson block has rank two
and annihilates all nine cusp vectors. The full
matrix is retained in
\texttt{bc\_ihara\_finite\_image\_certificate.npz}.

statement:
A finite precision determining the integral local kernel. Let $M_2=\bigwedge^2V$, and let
\[
 \mathcal D=M_2^c\oplus
       \ker(1+\rho(n)c:M_2\longrightarrow M_2)
\]
be the rank-$45$ lattice of normalized source cocycles
used in A.39. Define the actual Frobenius evaluation
\[
 E_\varphi:\mathcal D\longrightarrow M_2^c,
 \qquad E_\varphi(\gamma)=\gamma(\varphi_{17}),
 \qquad R=\ker E_\varphi.
\]
The integral operator
$B=(F_\varphi-1)|M_2^c$ has three-adic Smith
exponents
\[
 \underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{6},\quad
 \underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{7},\quad
 \underbrace{3,3}_{2},\quad
 \underbrace{4,\ldots,4}_{6}.
                                                               \tag{B.19.1}
\]
Identify $R/3R$ with its image in $\mathcal D/3\mathcal D$.
Then its exact finite-precision description is
\[
 \frac{R}{3R}
 =\operatorname{im}\left(
 \ker\left(
 \mathcal D/243\mathcal D
       \xrightarrow{\ E_\varphi\ }
 M_2^c/243M_2^c\right)
 \longrightarrow\mathcal D/3\mathcal D\right).
                                                               \tag{B.19.2}
\]
More explicitly, for every integral $d\in\mathcal D$
with $E_\varphi(d)\in243M_2^c$, put
\[
 h=B^{-1}E_\varphi(d)\in3M_2^c,
 \qquad \gamma=d-\delta h,
 \qquad (\delta h)(g)=g(h)-h.
                                                               \tag{B.19.3}
\]
Then $\gamma\in R$ and $\gamma\equiv d\pmod{3\mathcal D}$.
The matrix $B$ and the bound (B.19.1) are computed
in the attached certificate. Evaluating the separate
arithmetic matrix $E_\varphi\bmod243$ remains the
finite calculation needed to list the resulting
$24$-dimensional subspace individually.

statement:
An individually specified class-two target with no class-four lift. Use the actual arithmetic basis $m,n,c$ of A.38 and
A.31. Write the ten integral A.7 basis vectors as
\[
 \begin{split}
 (v_0,\ldots,v_7)
   &=(e_P,e_{Q_c},e_A,e_{\bar A},e_B,e_{\bar B},e_C,e_{\bar C}),\\
 v_8&=(\Psi(1,0)/3,(1,0)),\qquad
 v_9=(\Psi(0,1)/3,(0,1))
       \quad\text{in }L_\Psi\subset W_{\mathbb Q_3}\oplus T_{\mathbb Q_3}.
 \end{split}                                                \tag{B.20.1}
\]
Let $C_2$ be the actual action of $c$ on
$M_2=\bigwedge^2V$. Define the integral vectors
\[
 b_0=3v_8\wedge v_9+
       \sum_{i=0}^7
       \bigl(\Psi_{i,2}v_i\wedge v_8
             -\Psi_{i,1}v_i\wedge v_9\bigr),
 \qquad b=(1-C_2)b_0.                                     \tag{B.20.2}
\]
Here the columns of $\Psi$ are numbered one and two.
In the basis $v_i\wedge v_j$, $i<j$, all nonzero
coordinates of $b$ are the following; every other
coordinate is zero:
\[
 \begin{array}{cr|cr|cr}
 (i,j)&b_{ij}&(i,j)&b_{ij}&(i,j)&b_{ij}\\\hline
 (0,8)&-2&(1,8)&2&(2,6)&-1\\
 (2,7)&1&(2,8)&2&(2,9)&2\\
 (3,6)&1&(3,7)&-1&(3,9)&-2\\
 (4,6)&1&(4,7)&-1&(4,8)&-2\\
 (4,9)&-2&(5,6)&-1&(5,7)&1\\
 (5,9)&2&(6,8)&2&(6,9)&-2\\
 (7,8)&-2&(7,9)&2&(8,9)&6.
 \end{array}                                                \tag{B.20.3}
\]
The prescriptions
\[
             \gamma(m)=0,\qquad \gamma(n)=b,
             \qquad \gamma(c)=0                           \tag{B.20.4}
\]
define an actual continuous $M_2$-cocycle unramified
outside three. Let $s_{O,17}$ be the actual $O$-cuspidal
section with tangent parameter seventeen. In
$A=N/\gamma_3N$, put
\[
                        s_b(g)=\gamma(g)s_{O,17}(g).
                                                               \tag{B.20.5}
\]
This is an actual class-two section, with abelian
class $\kappa_{17}e_O$. Its restriction at seventeen
equals the specified local cuspidal section exactly.
It has a global lift to $N/\gamma_4N$, but no global
lift to $N/\gamma_5N$. Consequently it has no full,
metabelian, or marked-depth lift.

The projection of (B.20.4) to $\bigwedge^2T$ has
the exact generator values $0,6$. If
$a=\kappa_3(n)\in\mathbb Z_3^\times$ in this actual
source basis, this cocycle is $(6/a)\kappa_3$.
Only $a\equiv1\pmod3$ is used; its integral value
has not been replaced by one.

statement:
No arithmetic centralizer in the class-two geometric group. For every number field $L$ and every continuous section
$s:G_L\to A\rtimes G_L$,
\[
                 C_A(s(G_L))=1.                         \tag{C.1}
\]
The assertion uses the whole $G_L$, in contrast to the subgroup
$\ker\chi$ in B.4; the comparison map between the two assertions
is the inclusion of subgroups, which reverses inclusions of their
centralizers.

statement:
All restriction maps are injective and finite Galois descent is exact. For number fields $L\subset L'$, restriction is the injective
map of pointed sets
\[
 \operatorname{res}_{L'/L}:\operatorname{Sec}_L
                   \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sec}_{L'},
 \qquad [z]\longmapsto[z|_{G_{L'}}].                        \tag{C.2}
\]
For $L'/L$ finite Galois it identifies its source with precisely
the $\operatorname{Gal}(L'/L)$-fixed classes in its target.
Writing $\rho$ for the based action on $A$, the action by
$g\in G_L$ is represented by
\[
       (g\cdot z)(h)=\rho(g)z(g^{-1}hg),\quad h\in G_{L'}.
                                                               \tag{C.3}
\]
Thus the kernel of (C.2), as a pointed-set map, is its base
point, and its image in the invariant set is the entire set.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The action and fields of definition of germs. The set
\[
          \mathscr G=\varinjlim_{L\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}}
                                      \operatorname{Sec}_L
                                                               \tag{C.4}
\]
has a well-defined $G_{\mathbb Q}$-action obtained by
(C.3) together with conjugation of the field of definition.
Every transition map is injective.  Each germ has an open
stabilizer and a finite orbit.  For every number field $L$,
\[
       \operatorname{Sec}_L\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\
                                    \mathscr G^{G_L}.          \tag{C.5}
\]
In particular the image of $\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathbb Q}$
is exactly the fixed-germ set.  The fixed field of the
stabilizer of a germ is its smallest field of definition.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The R2 obstruction does not disappear as a germ. Let $c=9\kappa(3)\cup\beta$ be the nonzero R2 class
specified by LM7 (E.32f), so that in
$H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathbb Z_3(2))=
\mathcal R/d\mathcal R$ it is represented by
\[
 z_{q_j}=q_j-1\quad(j\ge3),\qquad z_q=0
                       \text{ at the other primes}.          \tag{C.6}
\]
For every finite number field $L$,
$\operatorname{res}_{L/\mathbb Q}(c)\ne0$.
In fact these restrictions all have infinite additive order.
Consequently $c$ gives a nonzero element of
$\varinjlim_L H^2_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathbb Z_3(2))$.
The vanishing assertion in the first sentence of Task C.4
is false.

statement:
Restriction is injective on the Tate-twist phantom subgroup. For $\mathbb Z_3(2)$ the kernel of the finite-coefficient
comparison map in R2 is torsion-free, and restriction
from $\mathbb Q$ to any finite number field is injective
on this kernel.  This extends C.4 from its particular
cup-product witness to every nonzero class in that
kernel.
