statement:
Complete class-two germ classification. Task C.1 requests the full explicit residue complex,
obstruction residues, convergence criterion, and fibers
over every number field $L$.  C.11 disproves a
verbatim pure-residue extension of Part A; C.12
gives the exact replacement, including the
finite-$S_L$ arithmetic class and the lift torsor.
C.13 evaluates the preceding cuspidally central
obstruction by the local quadratic pairings at the
places above three, with their global sum relation.
C.14 computes the finite-$S_L$ complexes by finite Galois
cochain matrices and Artin--Verdier duality, and C.15
evaluates the retained class by explicit compact-support
cup traces.  Together with the restricted-family condition
in C.12, these give the full number-field criterion and
fibers requested in Task C.1.
For Task C.2, C.1--C.3 give injective restriction,
the actual Galois action and exact descent.  Formula
(C.5) identifies $\operatorname{Sec}_L$ with all
$G_L$-fixed germs.
For Task C.3, C.8--C.9 prove injectivity of the point
map and separation from cusp germs.  C.10 gives the
nine disjoint cusp parameter spaces with their torsion
and Galois action.  C.16 evaluates every point's
abelian and central coordinates by finite algebraic
operations at each precision; C.17 is an explicit
nonzero central instance.  C.18 gives the exact
point-image set, its equivariance and its full
central membership criterion.  Its coordinate
maps retain the E36 origin and the lift-fiber
translation.  Finally C.4--C.5 and C.7 prove
that both specified phantom classes remain
nonzero after every finite number-field
extension and in the germ colimit, settling
Task C.4.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The intrinsic phantom obstruction also survives every finite extension. The nonzero obstruction in $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{\mathbb Q},\mathcal K)$
constructed in A.4 remains nonzero over every finite number
field and in the filtered colimit over all number fields.
More generally, restriction to every finite number field is
injective on the phantom subgroup for $\mathcal K$ computed
in A.2.

statement:
An exact tangent-line separation identity. Let $\ell_d$ be a row vector defining the flex tangent line at $d\in D$.
The nine rows can be chosen as
\[
 (1,\zeta^a,0),\quad(0,1,\zeta^a),\quad(\zeta^a,0,1)
 \qquad (a=0,1,2).
\]
Set $P_d=\ell_d^*\ell_d/2$, a rank-one Hermitian projector on
$\mathbb C^3$. The real-linear map
\[
 \operatorname{Herm}_3(\mathbb C)\longrightarrow\mathbb R^9,
 \qquad H\longmapsto\bigl(\operatorname{tr}(P_d H)\bigr)_d
\]
is an isomorphism, and
\[
 \sum_d P_d=3I_3,\qquad
 \operatorname{tr}(P_dP_e)=
 \begin{cases}1&d=e,\\1/4&d\ne e.\end{cases}
 \tag{C.8.1}
\]
The kernel after deleting coordinate $d$ is the line
$\mathbb R(4P_d-I_3)$. A positive semidefinite matrix with the
eight undeleted measurements of $vv^*$, where $v\ne0$ and
$\ell_d(v)=0$, is exactly $vv^*$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Injective point germs and their separation from cusp germs. The canonical map
\[
 U(\overline{\mathbb Q})\longrightarrow
 \varinjlim_L\operatorname{Sec}_L(N/\gamma_3N)
\]
is injective and $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant. Its image is
disjoint from all the cuspidal germs. Both assertions already
hold after projecting to the germ colimit of $H^1(G_L,V)$.
The smallest field of definition of a point germ is the field
of definition of the point.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The nine disjoint cusp germ packets and their Galois action. Define the abelian germ parameter group
\[
 \mathscr K=\varinjlim_{L\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}}
       H^1_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathbb Z_3(1))
   =\varinjlim_L\varprojlim_n L^\times/L^{\times3^n}.       \tag{C.10.1}
\]
All transition maps are restriction.  Choose at each cusp
$d\in D(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ the unit tangent for the parameter
$x/z$ when $x=0$, $y/z$ when $y=0$, and $z/x$ when $z=0$.
These choices are $G_{\mathbb Q}$-equivariant.
The map
\[
 \coprod_{d\in D(\overline{\mathbb Q})}\mathscr K
       \longrightarrow\mathscr G,
 \qquad (d,u)\longmapsto[s_{d,1}\text{ twisted by }u]
                                                               \tag{C.10.2}
\]
is injective, and its image is exactly the cuspidal germ set.
There are nine packets.  The $G_{\mathbb Q}$-action in these
coordinates is
\[
                         g(d,u)=(gd,gu),                     \tag{C.10.3}
\]
where $gu$ transports a Kummer class over $L$ to its class over
$gL$ by the field isomorphism $g:L\to gL$.
The parameter group has injective restriction maps, is divisible,
and has torsion subgroup canonically $\mu_{3^\infty}$, with its
usual Galois action.  In particular, distinct torsion parameters
and distinct cusp packets do not merge in the germ colimit.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The pure-residue computation over the rationals does not extend verbatim to every number field. Let
\[
       L=\mathbb Q(\zeta_3,\sqrt{10}),\qquad
       S_L=\{v:v\mid3\}\cup\{v:v\mid\infty\}.
\]
For the actual rank-forty-four module $\mathcal K$,
\[
                   H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K)\ne0.
                                                               \tag{C.11.1}
\]
Its inflation into $H^2_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathcal K)$ is
injective, and every one of its classes has zero
residue outside $S_L$.
Consequently the pure-residue isomorphism (A.1.3)
cannot be transported to this $L$ by replacing the
rational primes with its finite primes.  The
finite-$S_L$ complex is a necessary part of Task C.1.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The exact general number-field criterion with its retained arithmetic term. For any number field $L$, put $S_L=\{v\mid3,\infty\}$,
$A_v=\mathcal K(-1)$ and $D_v=F_v-1$ for $v\notin S_L$.
Let $\mathcal R_L(A)$ denote the families in these
integral lattices tending to zero three-adically.
Then there are exact maps
\[
\begin{aligned}
 0\longrightarrow H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K)
 &\xrightarrow{\rm inf}H^2_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathcal K)\\
 &\xrightarrow{\rm res}
       \mathcal R_L(A)/D\mathcal R_L(A)
       \longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}                                              \tag{C.12.1}
\]
\[
 H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}H^1_{\rm cts}(G_L,\mathcal K).             \tag{C.12.2}
\]
The quotient in (C.12.1) uses the actual image of $D$.
The first term is the inverse limit of the finite
groups $H^2(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K/3^n)$.

For a section of $N^{\rm cc}$ over $L$, take its
actual local path-origin residues $r_v$ by the
formula (A.8.3), with residue size $\#k(v)$ and the
restricted $G_L$-action.  Its intrinsic obstruction
vanishes exactly when both of the following tests hold:
\[
 y_v=-D_v^{-1}r_v\in A_v\text{ for every }v\notin S_L,
        \qquad (y_v)_v\in\mathcal R_L(A);                  \tag{C.12.3}
\]
\[
 \eta(s)=0\quad\text{in }H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K).
                                                               \tag{C.12.4}
\]
Here, once (C.12.3) holds, $\eta(s)$ is the unique
class whose inflation is the full continuous
obstruction of $s$.  Every nonempty class-two lift
fiber is a torsor under
$H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S_L},\mathcal K)$, with no further
geometric-stabilizer quotient.
This statement retains the finite-$S_L$ test; it
does not claim an evaluation of that test for
arbitrary $L$.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The initial cuspidally central obstruction over every number field. Let $L\subset\overline\Q$ be a number field and let
$\alpha\in H^1(G_L,V)$, with image $\beta\in H^1(G_L,T)$.
Orient $\bigwedge^2T\simeq\Z_3(1)$ by the commutator in
the once-punctured elliptic curve, and write $\omega$ for
this alternating pairing. For each $v\mid3$ define
\[
 q_v(\beta)=\tfrac12\operatorname{inv}_v
       \omega_*(\beta_v\smile\beta_v)\in\Z_3.
 \tag{C.13.1}
\]
Here $\operatorname{inv}_v:H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L_v},\Z_3(1))
\xrightarrow{\sim}\Z_3$ is the inverse limit of the
normalized local Brauer invariant maps. Then
\[
 \alpha\in\operatorname{im}
   \bigl(\operatorname{Sec}_L(N^{\rm cc})\to H^1(G_L,V)\bigr)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
             q_v(\beta)=0\text{ for every }v\mid3.
 \tag{C.13.2}
\]
The tuple satisfies $\sum_{v\mid3}q_v(\beta)=0$.
Every nonempty fiber is a torsor under
$H^1(G_L,\Z_3(1))=\varprojlim_n L^\times/(L^\times)^{3^n}$,
with no further stabilizer quotient. In particular, every
abelian section lifts to $N^{\rm cc}$ over a number field
having exactly one place above three, including $\Q$.
This statement makes no assertion that every tuple subject
to the displayed sum occurs as a self-pairing.
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.16,
folios 733v--736v, scans 172--178, formulas (371)--(379).}
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
An explicit finite Galois construction of the retained arithmetic groups. Fix a number field $L\subset\overline{\mathbb Q}$ and put
$S=\{v:v\mid3\}\cup\{v:v\mid\infty\}$.
For $n\ge1$ write
\[
 A_n=\mathcal K/3^n,\qquad
 A_n^D=\operatorname{Hom}(A_n,\mu_{3^n}),\qquad
 F_n=L(J_{E,D}[3^n],\mu_{3^n}),\qquad
 d_n=3^{44n}[F_n:L].                                      \tag{C.14.1}
\]
The homomorphisms in the dual have their usual contragredient
Galois action. Let $\Omega_n$ be the compositum, inside the
fixed algebraic closure, of all finite Galois extensions $E/L$
containing $F_n$, unramified outside $S$, and satisfying
$[E:L]\le d_n$. Put $G_n=\operatorname{Gal}(\Omega_n/L)$.
At each $v\mid3$ choose a prolongation to $\Omega_n$ and
write $D_{n,v}\le G_n$ for its decomposition subgroup.
These are finite fields and finite groups, obtained by the
bounded enumeration in the proof.

For a finite $G_n$-module $A$, use the finite matrices
\[
 \begin{split}
  (\delta^0 b)(g)&=g b-b,\\
  (\delta^1 z)(g,h)&=g z(h)-z(gh)+z(g).
 \end{split}                                               \tag{C.14.2}
\]
Define the following finite abelian groups by kernels and
images of these matrices:
\[
 U_n=\ker\bigl(\delta^1:\operatorname{Map}(G_n,A_n)
                   \to\operatorname{Map}(G_n^2,A_n)\bigr)
                      /\delta^0 A_n,                       \tag{C.14.3}
\]
and
\[
\begin{split}
 C_n={}&\{(z,(b_v)_{v\mid3}):
       \delta^1z=0,\ b_v\in A_n^D,\\
     &\hspace{26mm}z(g)=g b_v-b_v
             \text{ for }g\in D_{n,v}\}\big/
        \{(\delta^0 b,(b)_{v\mid3}):b\in A_n^D\}.
\end{split}                                                 \tag{C.14.4}
\]
In (C.14.4), $z$ ranges over all functions $G_n\to A_n^D$.
There are canonical identifications
\[
\begin{split}
 H^1(G_{L,S},A_n)&\simeq U_n,\qquad
 H^2(G_{L,S},A_n)\simeq C_n^\vee,\\
 H^1_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S},\mathcal K)&\simeq\varprojlim_n U_n,\qquad
 H^2_{\rm cts}(G_{L,S},\mathcal K)
       \simeq\varprojlim_n C_n^\vee .
\end{split}                                                 \tag{C.14.5}
\]
Here $C_n^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}(C_n,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)$;
the transition maps are induced by coefficient reduction
and its Cartier dual. Thus the arithmetic terms of C.12
are specified by finite arithmetic fields and finite matrices
at every precision. The construction applies to every $L$;
it does not assume that either displayed inverse limit is zero.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The complete number-field class-two test with its finite arithmetic evaluations. Let $s$ be a continuous section of $N^{\rm cc}$ over $L$.
Use the actual obstruction two-cocycle $o$ and its
origin-corrected residue family $r=(r_v)_{v\nmid3,\infty}$
from A.8, restricted to $G_L$. Write
$D_v=\operatorname{Frob}_v-1$ on $\mathcal K(-1)$.
First require
\[
 y_v=-D_v^{-1}r_v\in\mathcal K(-1),\qquad
 (y_v)_v\in\mathcal R_L(\mathcal K(-1)).                    \tag{C.15.1}
\]
The actual localization homotopy-fibre cycle $(o,y)$
then supplies, at each $n$, a two-cocycle
$\xi_n\in Z^2(G_{L,S},A_n)$, by the comparison below.
For every class represented by $(z,(b_v))$ in the
explicit finite group $C_n$ of C.14, choose a continuous
two-cochain $a$ with values in $\mu_{3^n}$ satisfying
\[
                        da=\xi_n\cup z.                    \tag{C.15.2}
\]
Such a cochain always exists. Define
\[
 \ell_n(s)(z,(b_v))
   =\sum_{v\mid3}\operatorname{inv}_v
       \bigl((\operatorname{res}_v\xi_n)\cup b_v
                          -\operatorname{res}_v a\bigr).
                                                               \tag{C.15.3}
\]
The expression in each local invariant is a two-cocycle.
Formula (C.15.3) is independent of all the auxiliary
cochain choices and is an element of $C_n^\vee$.
There is an exact criterion
\[
 s\text{ lifts to }N/\gamma_3N
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{(C.15.1) holds and }
        \ell_n(s)=0\text{ for every }n\ge1.                 \tag{C.15.4}
\]
Every nonempty fibre is a torsor under
$\varprojlim_n U_n$, with $U_n$ given by the finite
matrices (C.14.3), and no further geometric-stabilizer
quotient. Together with C.13 for the initial lift,
C.14--C.15 give the number-field version requested
in Task C.1: both the residue convergence and the
arithmetic test are retained.

statement:
Finite algebraic formulas for every point's abelian and central coordinates. Put $m=3^n$.  Two successive Kummer covers and a quotient
of their finite deck group construct a based finite cover
$X_n\to U$ with group
\[
 P_n=N/(N^{3^n}\gamma_3N).                                  \tag{C.16.1}
\]
Its multiplication, arithmetic action, transition maps,
and fibers at algebraic points are computed by finite
algebraic operations.  The tangential base point is the
specified $s=z/x$, tangent one.

Choose compatible lifts $y_1,\ldots,y_{10}$ of a
$\mathbb Z_3$-basis of $V$.  For every $A\in U(L)$ the
construction gives compatible finite cocycles
\[
 c_{A,n}(g)=(v_{A,n}(g),z_{A,n}(g))
 \in(V/3^n)\oplus(\bigwedge\nolimits^2V/3^n).                \tag{C.16.2}
\]
They are obtained by evaluating roots of rational
functions at $A$ and comparing the resulting fibers
with the Puiseux fiber at $O$.  Their inverse limit
is a continuous cocycle whose class is the class-two
point section of $A$.  Thus (C.16.2) evaluates all
forty-five central coordinates with their tangent origin.

statement:
An evaluated nonzero central point coordinate. Let $\alpha^3=2$, $\zeta=\zeta_3$, $\eta=\zeta_9$
with $\eta^3=\zeta$, and $L=\mathbb Q(\zeta,\alpha)$.
For $A=[1:-\alpha:1]\in U(L)$ an explicit quotient
of $P_1$ of order $27$ has zero abelian point
coordinates and central coordinate
\[
                  -\kappa_L(\zeta)\in
                    H^1(G_L,\mathbb F_3)                  \tag{C.17.1}
\]
in the prescribed unit-tangent origin at $O$.
This class is nonzero.

statement:
The point-image set and its exact central membership criterion. The point-image subset of the class-two germ set is
\[
 \left\{
   \left[\left(\varprojlim_n v_{A,n},
                   \varprojlim_n z_{A,n}\right)\right]:
                  A\in U(\overline{\mathbb Q})
 \right\},                                                \tag{C.18.1}
\]
where each finite function is algebraically evaluated
by (C.16.3)--(C.16.13).
This parametrization is injective, disjoint from the
nine packets (C.10.2), and equivariant for
$A\mapsto gA$.  Its stabilizer at $A$ is
$G_{\mathbb Q(A)}$.

Given a section and an algebraic point $A$, choose
a common number field $L$ of definition.
Let $d_n$ be the section cocycle in $P_n$ and
$c_{A,n}$ the evaluated cocycle above.
Their germs agree exactly when every finite set
\[
 \mathcal T_n=\{h\in P_n:
 d_n(g)=h^{-1}c_{A,n}(g)\rho_n(g)h
                         \text{ for all }g\in G_L\}
                                                               \tag{C.18.2}
\]
is nonempty.  Each test is a computation on a finite
Galois group.  Combined with the injective abelian
point map C.9, it gives a complete central
membership criterion for (C.18.1).

statement:
The weight-five image of the full profinite special group. For $\ell\geq5$, the dimension requested in Task D.1 has not been
determined here. The target computed in R8 is
\[
 (X+Y)\,\langle X^2,XY,Y^2\rangle_{\Q_\ell}[x,y].
\]
Statement D.21 proves that this image has dimension either $1$ or $3$:
the actual geometric $S_3$ preserves it, and its invariant gamma line
is already present by D.20. The remaining choice between $1$ and $3$
is not determined here.
notes: Unresolved statement; no completion certified.

statement:
The extra weight-nine direction for the full profinite gentle group. For $\ell\geq5$, we have neither constructed an element of
$\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0$ with leading metabelian coordinate outside
$\Q_\ell G_9$, nor proved that every such coordinate belongs to that line,
where
\[
 G_n=\frac{(X+Y)^n-X^n-Y^n}{XY},\qquad
 p_{\mathrm{extra}}=X^2Y^2(X+Y)^3.
\]
The requested choice between dimensions $1$ and $2$ remains open in
this return.
notes: Unresolved statement; no completion certified.

statement:
The finite pentagon comparison in the weight-nine stratum. At the compatible quotients
$PB_n/(\gamma_{11}PB_n\,PB_n^{101})$, for $n=3,4$, the complete
multiplier-one, weight-at-least-nine gentle shadow stratum has
$101^{37}$ elements. Exactly $101^2$ of these satisfy the complete
pentagon. Their degree-nine leading spaces have dimensions four and
one, respectively; their metabelian images have dimensions two and
one. The latter image is the line generated by $G_9$.
Statements D.7--D.8 give the finite comparison and an exact integer
certificate. Its characteristic-zero comparison, together with the
actual Galois lower bound in D.20, derives R9 in weight nine.
The enumeration is of the entire stratum that can contribute a
weight-nine leading term, with its degree-ten corrections; it is
not an enumeration of other multipliers or of lower leading weights.

statement:
Recomputed targets and the checked pentagon upper bound. The original rational program reproduces R8's four rows in weights
$1,\ldots,10$. In weight nine its invariant metabelian image has basis
$p_0=p_{\mathrm{extra}}$ and
\[
\begin{split}
 p_1={}&2X^7+8X^6Y+17X^5Y^2+23X^4Y^3\\
       &+23X^3Y^4+17X^2Y^5+8XY^6+2Y^7,
\end{split}
\qquad G_9=\frac{15}{2}p_0+\frac92p_1.
\]
The leading metabelian image of full $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ is contained
in $\Q_\ell G_n$ in positive odd weight $n$, and is zero in positive
even weight. In particular $p_{\mathrm{extra}}$ is excluded in weight
nine by this implication from the pentagon.

statement:
Cyclic-cover compatibility for every full profinite GT element. Let $H_N=\ker(\widehat F\to\Z/N)$, where $x\mapsto1$ and $y\mapsto0$.
The continuous homomorphism
\[
 \delta_N:H_N\longrightarrow\widehat F,
 \quad x^N\mapsto x,\quad y\mapsto y,\quad
 x^ayx^{-a}\mapsto1\quad(0<a<N)
\]
is defined on a profinite free basis. For every
$(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$, with the convention
$x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$, one has
\[
 \delta_N(f)=y^{c_N(f)}f,\qquad
 c_{MN}(f)=c_M(f)+c_N(f),
\]
where $c_N(f)$ is the $y$ coordinate of $\delta_N(f)$ in
$\widehat F^{\mathrm{ab}}$. These are Enriquez's Theorem 8.1 and
Remark 8.6 \cite{DE_Enriquez2007}.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The exact finite test and its remaining quantifier. For a finite-index normal subgroup $N_0\triangleleft B_3$ contained in
$PB_3$, the reduction maps of finite shadow sets satisfy
\[
 \im\bigl(\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0\to\mathrm{GT}(N_0)\bigr)
 =\bigcap_{K\subset N_0}
 R_{K,N_0}\bigl(\mathrm{GT}(K)\bigr),
\]
where $K$ ranges over all finite-index normal subgroups of $B_3$
contained in $N_0$. This is Dolgushev--Guynee, Theorem 5.2,
Corollary 5.4 and Proposition 5.5 \cite{DE_DolgushevGuynee2024},
with the full profinite identification supplied by Harbater--Schneps,
Main Theorem (a) \cite{DE_HarbaterSchneps2000}.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Compatible finite three- and four-strand shadows. Write $P_n=PB_n$, $p=101$, and
\[
 K_n=\gamma_{11}P_n\,P_n^p\triangleleft B_n\qquad(n=2,3,4),
 \qquad K_F=\gamma_{11}F\,F^p,
\]
where a power subgroup is generated by all the indicated powers.
All these groups are discrete until their finite quotients are taken.
We use $F=\langle x=A_{12},y=A_{23}\rangle\le P_3$ and the same
braid generators as in D.4. Let $\mathcal G_9$ be the finite gentle
shadows at $K_3$ with $m=0\pmod p$ and
$f\in\gamma_9(F/K_F)$. Let $\mathcal P_9\subset\mathcal G_9$ be
those satisfying the pentagon in $P_4/K_4$.
The logarithm bijection makes both sets vector spaces over
$\mathbb F_{101}$ and gives the following dimensions:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rr}
 &\mathcal G_9&\mathcal P_9\\\hline
 \log f\text{ in degrees }9,10&37&2\\
 \text{degree-nine projection}&4&1\\
 \text{degree-nine metabelian projection}&2&1.
\end{array}
\tag{D.7.1}
\]
The last right-hand space is exactly $\mathbb F_{101}G_9[x,y]$.
The induced three-strand kernel associated to $K_4$ in the finite
parenthesized-braid definition is exactly $K_3$, so
$\mathcal P_9$ consists of actual finite pentagon shadows in that
definition, not merely solutions in an unrelated Lie target.

statement:
An integer pentagon certificate and the weight-nine comparison. Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero or characteristic at
least five. In the free Lie algebra $L_k(X,Y)$ put
\[
 V_9=\{h\in L_k(X,Y)_9:
 h(X,Y)+h(Y,X)=0,\quad
 [X,h(X,Y)]=[X+Y,h(-X-Y,Y)]\}.
\]
Then $\dim V_9=4$, its metabelian image has dimension two,
and the infinitesimal pentagon map $P:V_9\to(\mathfrak t_4)_9$
has rank three. Its one-dimensional kernel has metabelian image
$k\,G_9(X,Y)[X,Y]$. The complete finite projection in D.7 is this kernel
when $k=\mathbb F_{101}$.
For every $\ell\ge5$, applying the corresponding rational
leading-term map to the full profinite pentagon equation and
using D.20 gives precisely $\mathbb Q_\ell G_9(X,Y)[X,Y]$ as the
weight-nine metabelian image of $\widehat{\rm GT}$ and of
the Galois image.

statement:
The checked Galois and full GT gamma line in every odd weight. For every prime $\ell\ge5$ and every odd integer $m\ge3$, the
rational leading metabelian image of $G_\Q$, and therefore of
$\widehat{\rm GT}$, is exactly
\[
 \Q_\ell G_m[x,y],\qquad
 G_m=\frac{(X+Y)^m-X^m-Y^m}{XY}.
 \tag{D.20.1}
\]
The leading image is zero in weight one and every positive even
weight. In particular R9 has dimensions
$0,0,1,0,1,0,1,0,1,0$ in weights one through ten, with the
specified coordinate $p(X,Y)[x,y]$.
This verifies the lower bound used in Tasks D.1--D.3; the full
gentle and special image questions in D.1--D.2 remain separate
questions about the displayed inclusion maps.
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.15,
manuscript pages 725--733 in the supplied transcription,
scans 156--170. The transcription does not establish the
recto/verso labels for this range.}

statement:
The weight-five full special image has dimension one or three. Let $\ell\ge5$, and let $\mathscr I_{5,\ell}$ be the rational
weight-five metabelian leading image of the full profinite group
$\operatorname{Out}^{\sharp}(\widehat F_2)$, with the source
filtration and leading map specified at the beginning of Part D.
Then
\[
             \dim_{\Q_\ell}\mathscr I_{5,\ell}\in\{1,3\}.
             \tag{D.21.1}
\]
In particular the intermediate value two offered in Task D.1 is
excluded. This statement leaves the choice between one and three
on the unresolved task ledger.
More precisely, the polynomial coordinate map
\[
 (X+Y)q(X,Y)[x,y]\longmapsto q(X,Y)
 \quad:\quad
 (X+Y)\Q_\ell[X,Y]_2[x,y]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
                    \Q_\ell[X,Y]_2
 \tag{D.21.2}
\]
identifies the target with the direct sum of the gamma line
$\Q_\ell(X^2+XY+Y^2)$ and an absolutely irreducible
two-dimensional $\mathfrak S_3$-module. The image in
(D.21.1) contains that line and is stable under this actual
geometric symmetry action.
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Manuscript comparison: \S51.15,
manuscript pages 725--733 in the supplied transcription,
scans 156--170; the full special-image question of LM7 D.13.}

statement:
Exact integral rank recovery and a finite-congruence limitation. Let $M$ be a finite free $\Z_\ell$-module and let $L\subset M$
be the image of a continuous homomorphism from a compact group
to the additive group of $M$. Write $L_n$ for its image under
the specified reduction $M\twoheadrightarrow M/\ell^nM$.
There are integers $e_1,\ldots,e_r\geq0$ such that
\[
 \log_\ell|L_n|=\sum_{i=1}^r\max(n-e_i,0),\qquad
 \dim_{\Q_\ell}(L\otimes\Q_\ell)
       =\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_\ell|L_n|}{n}=r.
 \tag{D.22.1}
\]
The successive difference of the displayed logarithms equals
$r$ for every $n>\max_i e_i$.

For each $a\geq1$ and each $\ell\geq5$, the actual
$\mathfrak S_3$-module $M=\Z_\ell[X,Y]_2$ of D.21 contains
two $\mathfrak S_3$-stable closed submodules with the same
image in $M/\ell^aM$, both containing $\Z_\ell q_0$, and
with rational dimensions one and three, respectively.
The corresponding two-dimensional target of D.2 contains
submodules with the same finite reduction and rational
dimensions one and two. These are explicit submodules;
we assert no realization of them as images of the profinite
sources in D.1 or D.2. They refute the inference of a
rational upper bound from one vanishing extra congruence
without further control of the integral image.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The complete abelian peripheral obstruction and chief-step count. Let
\[
 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E\xrightarrow{\pi}G
 \longrightarrow1
 \tag{D.23.2}
\]
be an extension of finite groups with $A$ elementary abelian of
characteristic $p$.  Choose generators $X_1,X_2$ of $E$, put
$X_3=(X_1X_2)^{-1}$ and $g_i=\pi(X_i)$, and denote the resulting
epimorphisms by $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ and
$q_G=\pi q_E$.  Let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ and
$\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times$ satisfy
$\alpha(g_i)\sim_G g_i^\lambda$ for all three indices.

Write $A_G=A/[E,A]$, use additive notation in $A$, and set
$C_i=C_G(g_i)$.  There are well-defined homomorphisms
\[
 \kappa_i:C_i\longrightarrow A_G,
 \qquad c\longmapsto[\widetilde c,X_i]\bmod[E,A],
 \qquad H=\sum_{i=1}^3\operatorname{im}\kappa_i.
 \tag{D.23.3}
\]
Choose $h_i\in G$ with
$\alpha(g_i)=h_i g_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}$, choose lifts
$H_i\in E$, and put
\[
 U_i=H_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1},\qquad r=U_1U_2U_3\in A.
 \tag{D.23.4}
\]
The class $o(\alpha,\lambda)=[r]\in A_G/H$ is independent of
these choices.  It vanishes exactly when there is a continuous
homomorphism $f:\widehat F\to E$ such that
\[
 \pi f=\alpha q_G,
 \qquad f(x_i)\sim_E X_i^\lambda\quad(1\leq i\leq3).
 \tag{D.23.5}
\]
The number of these literal homomorphisms is zero for nonzero
$o(\alpha,\lambda)$; for zero obstruction it is
\[
 C(E,G;X_1,X_2)=
 \frac{|A|^2|A_G|\prod_{i=1}^3|C_G(g_i)|}
 {|H|\prod_{i=1}^3|C_E(X_i)|}.
 \tag{D.23.6}
\]

When $A$ is an irreducible $\mathbf F_p[G]$-module, every nonempty
set in \textup{(D.23.5)} contains an epimorphism.  More precisely, let
$b(E,G;X_1,X_2)$ be the number of complements $C$ to $A$ in $E$
whose unique section $s_C:G\to C$ satisfies
$s_C(g_i)\sim_E X_i$ for every $i$.  For zero obstruction the number
of epimorphisms in \textup{(D.23.5)} is exactly $C-b>0$.
Thus every noncentral elementary-abelian chief step admits a
generating peripheral lift.  The possible abelian chief obstruction
is confined to a central kernel of order $p$.

The fixed-$h_i$ obstruction $[r]\in A_G$ is the relative extension
class under the explicit identification
\[
 H^2(\widehat F,\{S_1,S_2,S_3\};A_{\alpha q_G})
 \simeq A_G.
 \tag{D.23.7}
\]
Moreover $[r]$ comes from $H_2(G,\mathbf F_p)$ by the universal
central $p$-cover comparison in \textup{(D.23.12)} below.  In
particular $p\nmid|G|$ forces the obstruction to vanish.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
A peripheral-preserving finite automorphism with no peripheral lift. Let $S=\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbf F_{11})$ and
\[
 E=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbf F_{11})\times S,
 \qquad G=S\times S,
 \qquad\pi=(\text{central quotient},1).
 \tag{D.24.1}
\]
There is an explicit epimorphism $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$
for which the factor-swap automorphism
$\alpha:G\to G$, $(a,b)\mapsto(b,a)$, preserves each of the
three labelled peripheral conjugacy classes with multiplier one,
but no homomorphism \textup{(D.23.5)} exists.  Its obstruction is
the nonidentity element of $\ker\pi=\{(I,1),(-I,1)\}$.

The maximal pro-$\ell$ quotients of both $E$ and $G$ are trivial
for every prime $\ell$.  More precisely, for any two-generated
finite $\ell$-group $L$ with a specified generating triple
$l_1l_2l_3=1$ and any multiplier-one peripheral automorphism
$\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$, the corresponding product
quotient has maximal pro-$\ell$ quotient exactly $L$.
The automorphism $\alpha\times\beta$ of $G\times L$ has no
peripheral lift to $E\times L$, whereas $1_G\times\beta$ has
an explicit generating peripheral lift.  Thus the same prescribed
finite pro-$\ell$ component has both an obstructed and an admitted
choice of perfect component in this example.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
An order-five peripheral cycle obstructed by a central kernel of order two. There are finite groups
\[
 E\xrightarrow{\pi}G=A_8^5,\qquad |\ker\pi|=2,
 \tag{D.25.1}
\]
an epimorphism $q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$, and a
multiplier-one, labelled peripheral automorphism
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ of order five, such that
none of $\alpha,\alpha^2,\alpha^3,\alpha^4$ has a weak
peripheral lift through $\pi$.  The kernel is central and its
obstruction group in D.23 is exactly $\mathbf F_2$.
Consequently taking a $5$-adic unit power cannot remove this
obstruction.  In particular the order of the obstruction group
does not, by itself, bound the exponent of a power that removes
a pointed peripheral lifting obstruction.

Both groups in \textup{(D.25.1)} are perfect, and their maximal
pro-five quotients are trivial.  Thus this counterexample
corrects a proposed lifting argument; it imposes no restriction
on a nonzero pro-five leading coordinate in D.1.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The exact covering restriction of the central peripheral obstruction. Keep the finite groups, epimorphism $q_G:\widehat F\to G$,
factor-swap automorphism $\alpha$, and central extension
$\pi:E\to G$ of D.24.  Put $\theta=\alpha q_G$ and
$S_i=\overline{\langle x_i\rangle}$, with
$x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}$.  For any open subgroup
$H\leq\widehat F$ of index $d$, take representatives
$t\in F=\langle x_1,x_2\rangle$ of
$H\backslash\widehat F/S_i$ and set
\[
 e_{i,t}=[S_i:S_i\cap t^{-1}Ht],\qquad
 h_{i,t}=t x_i^{e_{i,t}}t^{-1},\qquad
 S_{i,t}=\overline{\langle h_{i,t}\rangle}\leq H.
 \tag{D.26.1}
\]
Let $b_H$ be the number of these induced peripheral subgroups.
The number of continuous homomorphisms $v:H\to E$ satisfying
\[
       \pi v=\theta|_H,\qquad
       v(h_{i,t})\sim_E X_i^{e_{i,t}}
                  \quad\text{for every }(i,t)
 \tag{D.26.2}
\]
is exactly
\[
 \begin{cases}
  0,&d\text{ odd},\\
  2^{\,d+2-b_H},&d\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{D.26.3}
\]
These are literal weak lifts with the fixed base map; no
surjectivity or quotient by conjugation is imposed on the count.

In particular every cover of odd index retains the nonzero
peripheral obstruction of D.24.  For every odd prime $\ell$,
this includes every open subgroup obtained as the inverse image
of a subgroup of a finite $\ell$-group quotient of $\widehat F$.
The exact map controlling this assertion is restriction
\[
\begin{split}
 H^2_{\cts}(\widehat F,\{S_i\};\F_2)&\longrightarrow
           H^2_{\cts}(H,\{S_{i,t}\};\F_2),\\
                   \F_2\ni a&\longmapsto d a\in\F_2,
\end{split}
 \tag{D.26.4}
\]
where both identifications use the sum of the oriented boundary
coordinates.  Thus passage to deeper covers of odd index cannot
solve this specified finite peripheral problem.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Exact coupled fibres over normalized finite pro-five shadows. There are explicit two-generated finite groups
\[
 E_0\xrightarrow{\pi_0}G_0\xrightarrow{\rho}C_5,
 \qquad |\ker\pi_0|=2,
 \tag{D.27.1}
\]
whose respective kernels over $C_5$ are perfect, and in which
$C_5$ acts nontrivially on those kernels by permutation of five
simple factors in each of five rows.  The groups have an
order-five, multiplier-one peripheral automorphism
$R\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_0)$ inducing the identity on $C_5$.
Each of $R,R^2,R^3,R^4$ is obstructed at the central kernel in
\textup{(D.27.1)}.

Here is their exact comparison with a prescribed pro-five
component.  Let $L=\langle l_1,l_2\rangle$ be a finite
$5$-group with an epimorphism
$\eta:L\to C_5=\langle t\rangle$ satisfying
$\eta(l_1)=t$, $\eta(l_2)=1$, and put
$l_3=(l_1l_2)^{-1}$.  Let $\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$
be specified by the peripheral equalities
\[
 \beta(l_1)=l_1,\qquad
 \beta(l_2)=f^{-1}l_2f,\quad \eta(f)=1,
 \qquad\beta(l_3)=h l_3h^{-1}.
 \tag{D.27.2}
\]
The condition on $f$ holds in particular for the usual
normalized multiplier-one form with $f\in L'$.
Define the actual fibre products
\[
 E_L=E_0\times_{C_5}L,
 \qquad G_L=G_0\times_{C_5}L.
 \tag{D.27.3}
\]
The paired source generators give epimorphisms
$\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E_L\twoheadrightarrow G_L$,
and the coordinate maps $E_L\to L$ and $G_L\to L$ are their
maximal pro-five quotient maps.  The automorphism
\[
 \alpha_-=(R,\beta)\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_L)
 \tag{D.27.4}
\]
has the prescribed three peripheral conjugacy classes and
has no weak peripheral lift to $E_L$.  On the same quotient
and over the same $\beta$, the automorphism
$\alpha_+=(1,\beta)$ has the explicit generating peripheral
lift $(1,\beta)\in\operatorname{Aut}(E_L)$.

The construction includes an explicit nonidentity $\beta$ of
order five on a finite two-generated $5$-group, given in
\textup{(D.27.15)--(D.27.18)} below.  Thus the perfect kernel,
its action by the quotient, and the prescribed pro-five
automorphism can all be nontrivial.  The admitted branch is
proved for every datum \textup{(D.27.2)}; these coupled
quotients therefore do not exclude such a prescribed
pro-five shadow.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Generating relative lifts for transitive $A_5$ wreath kernels. Let $D\leq\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a transitive finite
$5$-group, let $n=|\Omega|\geq25$, and let
$q:\widehat F=\langle x_1,x_2\rangle\twoheadrightarrow D$
be an epimorphism.  Put $x_3=(x_1x_2)^{-1}$ and $d_i=q(x_i)$.
Assume that each of the three permutations $d_i$ has no fixed
point on $\Omega$.  Give $\Omega$ its right $D$-action, and
write
\[
 M=A_5^{\Omega},\qquad
 (d\cdot a)(\omega)=a(\omega d),\qquad W=M\rtimes D.
 \tag{D.28.1}
\]
For every three elements $U_i\in W$ above $d_i$ there exist
$a_i\in M$ such that
\[
 V_i=a_iU_ia_i^{-1},\qquad
 V_1V_2V_3=1,\qquad\langle V_1,V_2\rangle=W.
 \tag{D.28.2}
\]
Equivalently, every such finite relative lifting problem has
a generating solution, with the three base conjugators fixed.
The kernel $M$ is a nonabelian chief factor: it is a product
of nonabelian simple groups, and $D$ permutes its factors
transitively.

In particular this applies to the regular action of every
noncyclic two-generated finite $5$-group $D$.  It also has
the following exact coupled consequence.  Let $L$ be a finite
$5$-group with epimorphism $\eta:L\to D$, and suppose
specified epimorphisms from $\widehat F$ to $W$ and $L$
have the same projection to $D$.  Let
$\beta\in\operatorname{Aut}(L)$ induce an automorphism
$\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$, and suppose its three
source peripheral images satisfy
\[
       \beta(l_i)=h_i l_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}
       \quad(1\leq i\leq3),\qquad
       \lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times.
 \tag{D.28.3}
\]
Then $\beta$ has a generating peripheral lift from
$\widehat F$ to the actual fibre product $W\times_D L$,
over the map $\beta q_L$, with the same multiplier
$\lambda$ and with the given $h_i$ retained in the
$L$-coordinates of its conjugators.

statement:
Exact peripheral count invariance for every $A_5$ chief step over an odd-order group. Let
\[
 1\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow E\xrightarrow{\pi}D
 \longrightarrow1,
 \qquad A\simeq A_5^{\Omega},
 \tag{D.29.1}
\]
be a finite extension, with $D$ of odd order and $A$ a
nonabelian chief factor of $E$.  Let
$q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ be an epimorphism,
$X_i=q_E(x_i)$, $q=\pi q_E$, and $d_i=q(x_i)$.
Let $q_1:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D$ be any
epimorphism, let $\lambda\in\widehat\Z^\times$, and
let $h_i\in D$ be specified elements such that
\[
           q_1(x_i)=h_i d_i^\lambda h_i^{-1}.
 \tag{D.29.2}
\]
choose any lifts $H_i\in E$ of $h_i$.
There is an epimorphism $f:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$
such that
\[
 \pi f=q_1,
 \qquad
 f(x_i)=a_iH_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1}a_i^{-1}
              \quad\text{for some }a_i\in A.
 \tag{D.29.3}
\]
The number of these literal epimorphisms is exactly the
number for $(q_1,\lambda,h_1,h_2,h_3)=(q,1,1,1,1)$.
In particular it is positive.  There is no degree or
fixed-point restriction on the transitive factor action
on $\Omega$.

The same assertion holds in every actual fibre product
$E\times_D L$, for a finite odd-order group $L$ and a
prescribed peripheral epimorphism $q_{L,1}:\widehat F\to L$
over $q_1$, relative to the original source epimorphism
$q_L:\widehat F\to L$: there is a generating lift over
$q_{L,1}$, with its specified peripheral conjugators
retained in the $L$-coordinate.  Here both maps to $L$
compose to the indicated maps to $D$, and the new
peripheral values are the specified conjugates of the
$\lambda$th powers of the original ones.
Thus every $A_5$ chief extension over a
finite odd-order group, including its coupled pullbacks, admits
all the peripheral shadows described in
\textup{(D.29.2)--(D.29.3)}.
In particular this applies over every finite $\ell$-group
for every odd prime $\ell$.

statement:

The number of these literal epimorphisms equals the

In particular it is positive.  There is no restriction
on the order of $D$, the degree of its factor action,

statement:
A proper-lift obstruction and its complete forgetful fibre. There is an actual chief extension
\[
 1\longrightarrow\operatorname{Inn}(A_6)
 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(A_6)
 \xrightarrow{\pi}\mathbf F_2^2\longrightarrow1
 \tag{D.31.1}
\]
and a generating peripheral triple $(X,Y,Z)$ of
orders $(2,8,8)$ such that the following holds.
Put $d_1=\pi(X)$, $d_2=\pi(Y)$, and
$d_3=d_1+d_2$.  With the same base epimorphism
$q_1=q_0$, multiplier $\lambda=1$, and prescribed
base conjugators
\[
                    (h_1,h_2,h_3)=(0,0,d_1),
 \tag{D.31.2}
\]
there are exactly ninety weak lifts and no
epimorphic lift.  Every weak lift has image
isomorphic to
\[
       C_8\rtimes_5 C_2
       =\langle r,s:r^8=s^2=1,\ srs^{-1}=r^5\rangle.
 \tag{D.31.3}
\]
The original choice $(h_1,h_2,h_3)=(0,0,0)$
has exactly 360 lifts, all epimorphic.

More precisely, write
$h_i=p_i d_1+q_i d_2$, with $p_i,q_i\in\mathbf F_2$.
The complete prescribed-conjugator count is
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 q_1+p_2+p_3+q_3&\text{weak lifts}&\text{epimorphic lifts}\\\hline
 0&360&360\\
 1&90&0.
 \end{array}
 \tag{D.31.4}
\]
Thus each row occurs for 32 of the 64 possible
base-centralizer triples.  Forgetting the
prescribed base conjugators gives a union of
1800 weak lifts and 1440 epimorphic lifts.
These form exactly two simultaneous
$\operatorname{Aut}(A_6)$-conjugacy orbits, of
sizes 1440 and 360, respectively.  The first is
the orbit of the original generating triple.
In particular the ordinary peripheral lift
fibre is nonempty.

Both groups in \textup{(D.31.1)} have trivial
maximal pro-five quotient.  For every finite
five-group $L$ and every specified
multiplier-one peripheral automorphism $\beta$
of its given two-generated source quotient,
the actual products of \textup{(D.31.1)}
with $L$ have maximal pro-five quotient $L$.
Over the same base shadow
$1_{\mathbf F_2^2}\times\beta$ they have both
the obstructed prescribed-conjugator branch
above and an explicit admitted branch.

an actual source epimorphism

projection of $\mathcal D$, conjugated
in the added $A_6$ factor, and has image

statement:

       \xrightarrow{\pi}D\longrightarrow1,

be a finite extension, with a given epimorphism
$q_E:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow E$ and

are $d_i$.  Let $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$
have odd order $m$ and satisfy

peripherals.  There is an actual automorphism
$\widetilde\alpha$ of $E$, of order $m$,
covering $\alpha$, fixing $S$ pointwise, and
satisfying

                    \widetilde\alpha(X_i)\in X_i^E.
 \tag{D.33.2}

order five cannot occur at a single
$A_6$ kernel.

statement:
An exact characteristic Magnus target and all three ordinary outer parameters. For every \(n\geq1\) there is an explicitly specified characteristic
finite quotient

 |P_n|=5^{17n+2},

which is metabelian of nilpotency class six.  It has
\(P_n^{\rm ab}\simeq(\mathbf Z/5^{n+1})^2\),
derived subgroup \((\mathbf Z/5^n)^{15}\), and centre
\(\gamma_6P_n\simeq(\mathbf Z/5^n)^5\).
Its kernel is fully invariant, by an explicit Fox substitution map.
Coefficient reduction gives onto maps \(P_{n+1}\to P_n\).

There is a specified injective homomorphism

 \qquad (A,B,C)\longmapsto[\beta_{A,B,C}],
 \tag{D.37.2}

whose representatives fix \(x_1\) and have actual multiplier-one

including all inner automorphisms of the finite quotient.

of order five of the characteristic group of order \(5^{19}\).

lifting question.  No assertion that a non-gamma parameter in

statement:
Actual automorphisms and every generating lift at the first coprime characteristic cover. Let \(q:\widehat F\twoheadrightarrow D\) be an epimorphism to a
finite group, let \(K=\ker q\), and let \(p\nmid |D|\).
Put
\[
 \Phi_p(K)=\overline{K^p[K,K]},\qquad
 E=\widehat F/\Phi_p(K),\qquad
 M=K/\Phi_p(K),\qquad n=|D|.
 \tag{D.39.1}

Then \(E\) is finite of order \(n p^{n+1}\), and \(M\) is the
actual \(D\)-module of first homology of the regular pants cover.
If \(K\) is characteristic in \(\widehat F\), so is
\(\Phi_p(K)\).

Write \(X_i\) for the images of the three peripheral generators
in \(E\), \(d_i=q(x_i)\), and \(e_i=\operatorname{ord}(d_i)\).
For every \(\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)\),
\(\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbf Z}^{\times}\), and specified

                 \alpha(d_i)=h_i d_i^\lambda h_i^{-1},
 \tag{D.39.2}
\]
there is an actual automorphism \(\widetilde\alpha\) of \(E\)
covering \(\alpha\) such that, for any chosen lifts \(H_i\) of

\[
 \widetilde\alpha(X_i)
       =a_iH_iX_i^\lambda H_i^{-1}a_i^{-1}
                     \quad\text{with }a_i\in M.
 \tag{D.39.3}
\]
Every generating source lift above \(\alpha q\) factors
through an automorphism of this same \(E\).

Let \(B\subset M\) be the boundary submodule and \(C=M/B\).
The complete fibre with the base conjugators \(h_i\) fixed
has, after stated linear choices, the parameter set
\[
 (M/M^D)\ \times\
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C,B)\ \times\
 \operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C).
 \tag{D.39.4}
\]
Its literal cardinality is
\[
 p^{n-1}
 \bigl|\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C,B)\bigr|
 \bigl|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbf F_p[D]}(C)\bigr|.
 \tag{D.39.5}
\]
Allowing every ordinary base conjugator multiplies this
cardinality by
\[
                       \prod_{i=1}^3
                       \frac{|C_D(d_i)|}{e_i}.
 \tag{D.39.6}
\]
These formulas count literal generating source maps, or
equivalently actual automorphisms of \(E\), before taking

statement:
The full profinite GT CM image. We have not determined whether full $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ reaches
the extra CM coset. The finite tests in E.6 impose consequences of
the pentagon established in D.5. E.17 evaluates the complete group
pentagon in the specified pure four-strand quotient of order $5184$.
It excludes fifteen of the twenty-four retained $G_6$ representatives,
but its rank-one affine equation has actual generating solutions in
every whole CM matrix fibre, simultaneously satisfying the class-two
cusp obstructions of E.11. E.18 retains the next central Ferrari
layer in a pure quotient of order $15552$: its pentagon has the
same zero sets on all whole affine fibres, and all twenty-four
retained words still generate the order-$648$ Ferrari image.
E.19 imposes the modulus-nine pentagon together with the complete
three-strand hexagons on the exact induced core. Each retained
point has one compatible correction in the full three-dimensional
commutator correction image, with generation verified in both
targets.
The missing step is compatibility through
all four-strand quotients. No positive or negative conclusion for
Task E.3 follows from the surviving finite candidates.
The primary comparison in
\cite[Proposition~4.4 and Theorem~4.16]{DE_NakamuraTsunogaiYasuda2010}
constructs the triangle-cover Tate action for full
$\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ but identifies it with the normalizer
$h$-coordinate on the Galois subgroup. The required comparison
of these two actions on the entire source remains unproved here.
The newer action of
\cite[Theorem~1.1]{DE_LochakNakamuraSchneps2026}
is defined on the profinite mapping class groups of type $(g,0)$
and $(g,1)$; its Section~8 explicitly leaves compatibility with
the indicated cutting homomorphisms unresolved for full
$\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. It does not provide the needed CM
comparison in the checked statements.

statement:

LM7 D.26. Each of its twelve extra CM pairs admits a compatible family
of shadows through the quotients $G_j$, with a coherently chosen
level-six cusp gauge and multiplier $\lambda\equiv1\pmod{72}$.
The family of kernels $K_j$ fails to be cofinal among the finite-index
normal subgroups of $B$ lying below $K_6$.

statement:
All certified shadows survive an explicit $A_5$ refinement. Define $a:B\twoheadrightarrow A_5$ by
$a(s)=(12)(34)$ and $a(r)=(135)$, and put
\[
 J_{A_5}=K_6\cap\ker a.
\]
The diagonal map induces an isomorphism
$B/J_{A_5}\simeq G_6\times A_5$. Its kernel does not contain
$[N_B,N_B]$. Every one of E.1's 24 certified shadows extends to a
shadow at the inverse image of $J_{A_5}$ in $B_3$. All twelve extra
CM coordinates survive this finite test.

statement:
Five simultaneous finite cyclic-cover tests preserve all 24 candidates. Let $f_0\in F'$ be the explicit gauged word of any E.1 certificate,
and let $q_F:F\twoheadrightarrow H=q(F)$ be the matrix quotient.
There is one word $k\in[N_B,N_B]$ such that $f_*=f_0k$ has the
same image as $f_0$ in $G_6$ and, simultaneously for all
$N\in\{2,3,4,6,12\}$, satisfies
\[
 q_F\delta_N(f_*)=q_F(y)^{c_N(f_*)}q_F(f_*),
 \qquad c_N(f_*)\text{ read modulo }6.
\]
It can be chosen also to satisfy, modulo six,
$c_4=2c_2$, $c_6=c_2+c_3$, and $c_{12}=2c_2+c_3$.
These are assertions in the listed finite targets.

statement:
All 24 candidates lift through the specified $S_3$ core. Fix the free basis $n_1,\ldots,n_{97}$ of $N_B$ given by the
fundamental cycles in E.1, ordered by the omitted-edge order in its
program. Let $\rho:N_B\twoheadrightarrow S_3$ send $n_1,n_2$ to
two different transpositions and the other basis elements to $1$.
Put
\[
 J=\operatorname{core}_B(\ker\rho\cap K_6),
 \qquad D_J=B/J.
\]
There is an exact sequence of finite groups
\[
 1\longrightarrow (\Z/3)^{288}\longrightarrow D_J
       \longrightarrow G_6\longrightarrow1.
\]
The cusp $t$ has order $72$ in $D_J$. Each of E.1's 24 certified
shadows is the reduction of a shadow at the inverse image of $J$ in
$B_3$, with multiplier one. All twelve extra CM shadows consequently
survive this first requested nonabelian refinement.

statement:
Finite-factor conjugacy for the full profinite gentle action. Every $g=(\lambda,f)\in\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0$ induces a continuous
automorphism of $\widehat B=C_2\amalg C_3$ sending $s$ to a conjugate
of $s$ and $r$ to a conjugate of $r^{\lambda\bmod3}$.
For $\lambda\equiv1\pmod3$, the conjugators can be chosen in
$\widehat F=\ker(\widehat B\to S_3)$.

statement:
An explicit common refinement removes all twelve recorded extra shadows. Number the 24 E.1 certificates from zero in their stored source order,
retaining exactly the records containing \texttt{mod6\_beta\_cycles}.
The exact gentle-shadow fibres of the two projections have the following
nonempty instances among these certificates:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|rr}
\text{refinement}&\text{surviving certificate indices}
 &\text{compatible}&\text{extra}\\\hline
 D_3\to G_6&0,1,2,3&2&2\\
 D_2\to G_6&0,16&1&1\\
 D_*\to G_6&0&1&0.
\end{array}
\]
The extra indices are
$1,2,4,7,9,10,12,15,16,19,21,22$.
Consequently none of the twelve recorded extra shadows is in the
image of $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}_0$, and none is in the image of
$\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$. This excludes those specified finite
shadows, while E.2 asks about all shadows in their CM matrix fibres.

statement:
The affine sizes of the CM matrix fibres. For each of the 24 admissible CM matrix pairs and multiplier one
modulo 72, the cusp-preserving changes of its two homology
conjugators form affine spaces of dimensions 98 over $\F_2$ and
97 over $\F_3$. Quotienting by the changes that leave both generator
images fixed gives dimensions 17 and 18. Quotienting further by
simultaneous conjugation by cusp powers gives dimensions 16 and 17.
The finite classification modulo all inner conjugations by the
centralizer of $t$ in $C/pC$ has dimensions 8 and 9.
Invertibility of the resulting action on $C/pC$ is an additional
condition in each of these spaces.

statement:
Every admissible CM matrix fibre has a replacement at the common refinement. Each of the 24 admissible CM matrix pairs of E.1 is attained by a
gentle shadow at $\widetilde J_*$, where $J_*=J_2\cap J_3$ is the
explicit refinement of E.9. In particular all twelve extra CM
\emph{matrix fibres} have nonempty image from this refinement,
although their twelve original recorded representatives are excluded
by E.9. The new witnesses are finite shadows; their membership in
the full profinite image is still to be determined.

statement:
All admissible CM pairs lift through the whole class-two three-primary tower. For every admissible CM matrix pair in E.1 there is a compatible
family of gentle shadows through all quotients
\[
 B/\bigl((\gamma_3N\,N^{3^k})\cap(N'N^2)\bigr),\qquad k\geq1,
\]
with multiplier one and that CM pair. Thus all twelve extra matrix
fibres survive this entire tower. This assertion concerns matrix
fibres with a coherent cusp gauge; it does not assert that an
independently chosen normalized finite representative extends.

statement:
Every CM matrix fibre survives the common exponent-eight refinement. Put
\[
 J_{8,3}=(\gamma_3N\,N^8)\cap(\gamma_3N\,N^3).
\]
This is a normal finite-index subgroup of $B$, contained in $J_*$
of E.9. Its inverse image in $B_3$ is normal, has finite index,
and is contained in $PB_3$. Each of the 24 admissible CM matrix
pairs of E.1 is attained by a gentle shadow at this refinement,
with multiplier one modulo $288$. In particular every one of
the twelve extra CM matrix fibres remains nonempty here.

statement:
Every CM matrix fibre survives the common exponent-sixteen refinement. Let $J_{16,3}=(\gamma_3N\,N^{16})\cap(\gamma_3N\,N^3)$.
Its inverse image in $B_3$ is a finite-index normal subgroup
contained in $PB_3$. Every one of the 24 admissible CM matrix
pairs of E.1 occurs as a gentle shadow at this refinement,
with multiplier one modulo $576$.

statement:
Every admissible CM pair survives the entire relative class-two tower. For each of the 24 admissible CM matrix pairs there is a
compatible family of gentle shadows at the inverse images
in $B_3$ of
\[
             J_j=\gamma_3N\,N^j\qquad(6\mid j),
 \tag{E.15.1}
\]
ordered by divisibility, with multiplier $\lambda=1$.
All twelve extra matrix fibres therefore survive this
entire tower. The assertion specifies matrix fibres;
it does not assert extension of the particular normalized
words retained in E.13 or E.14.

statement:
Simultaneous extension through every nonabelian simple quotient. Let $\Sigma$ be any finite collection of epimorphisms
$\theta:B\twoheadrightarrow S_\theta$ to nonabelian finite
simple groups, and put
\[
 K_{j,\Sigma}=\gamma_3N\,N^j\cap
                \bigcap_{\theta\in\Sigma}\ker\theta,
 \qquad 6\mid j.
 \tag{E.16.1}
\]
Every one of the 24 CM matrix pairs has a compatible family
of gentle shadows at the inverse images of these subgroups
in $B_3$, with multiplier one, as $j$ increases by
divisibility and $\Sigma$ increases by inclusion.
Thus the class-two families of E.15 extend simultaneously
through all these nonabelian simple quotients.
For each fixed epimorphism $B\twoheadrightarrow R$ to
an arbitrary finite perfect group, they also extend
compatibly in $j$ through
$\gamma_3N\,N^j\cap\ker(B\to R)$.

The finite solvable quotient
$B/(\gamma_4N\,N^5)$ is not a quotient, through the natural
map from $B$, of any $B/K_{j,\Sigma}$. This gives a precise
remaining finite comparison outside this enlarged family.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
The complete Ferrari-homology pentagon test and its affine fibres. Put $H_3=\F_3^2\rtimes\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_3)$, with the
standard left action on column vectors. The assignments
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \rho_4(\sigma_1)&=(0,A),&
 A&=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\\
 \rho_4(\sigma_2)&=(0,B),&
 B&=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-1&1\end{pmatrix},\\
 \rho_4(\sigma_3)&=(e_1,A)
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{E.17.1}
\]
define an epimorphism $B_4\to H_3$.
Let $L_4=\ker\rho_4\cap PB_4$. Then $L_4$ is normal
in $B_4$, is contained in $PB_4$, and
$|B_4/L_4|=5184$.

The complete pentagon in $PB_4/L_4$ is a well-defined
condition on the $G_6$ conjugator coordinate used in E.1.
Among the 24 particular $G_6$ representatives retained
in E.14, exactly nine satisfy it. They have indices
\[
             3,4,5,7,8,14,15,17,23;
 \tag{E.17.2}
\]
the extra-coset indices among these are $4,7,15$.
The other fifteen particular representatives cannot
be projections of full $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ elements.

Every one of the 24 \emph{whole CM matrix fibres}, however,
contains a gentle $G_6$ shadow with multiplier one
whose actual commutator word satisfies this pentagon.
In the 18-parameter three-primary presentation of E.10,
before quotienting by cusp conjugations, its equation
is one nonzero affine linear equation. Its solution
space has dimension 17 and contains points with full
generation rank 97 and with vanishing class-two cusp
obstructions of E.11. This is a finite pentagon test;
no lift through all four-strand quotients is asserted.

statement:
The next Ferrari central layer adds no equation on these affine fibres. Let $\mathcal H_3$ be the class-two exponent-three free group on two
generators, in coordinates $(u,v,z)\in\F_3^3$ with multiplication
\[
 (u,v,z)(u',v',z')=
 (u+u',v+v',z+z'+2(uv'-vu')).
\]
The standard action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_3)$ on $(u,v)$ fixes $z$.
Put $\widetilde H_3=\mathcal H_3\rtimes\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_3)$.
The assignments
\[
 \sigma_1\longmapsto((0,0,0),A),\qquad
 \sigma_2\longmapsto((0,0,0),B),\qquad
 \sigma_3\longmapsto((1,0,2),A)
 \tag{E.18.1}
\]
define an epimorphism $\widetilde\rho_4:B_4\to\widetilde H_3$,
where $A,B$ are those in (E.17.1). The normal pure kernel
$\widetilde L_4=\ker\widetilde\rho_4\cap PB_4$ has index $15552$.
Reduction of the Heisenberg central coordinate gives the precise
quotient $\widetilde H_3\to H_3$ of E.17.

All six evaluations used in E.17 still factor through $G_6$.
On each of the 24 whole affine CM fibres, their joint parameter
image has dimension two, with exactly the same kernel as in E.17.
The complete pentagon has exactly the same zero set on this
image: three of its nine points. Every retained E.17 literal
witness satisfies the complete pentagon and all three braid
relations in $\widetilde H_3$, and its three braid images generate
that group. Thus this additional central layer preserves all
24 nonempty fibres and introduces no further affine equation.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Complete compatible corrections at the modulus-nine Ferrari test. For $R=\mathbb Z/9$, let $\mathcal H(R)$ have coordinates
$(u,v,z)\in R^3$ and multiplication
\[
 (u,v,z)(u',v',z')=
 (u+u',v+v',z+z'+\tfrac12(uv'-vu')),
 \qquad \tfrac12=5\text{ in }R.
\]
Put $H_9=\mathcal H(R)\rtimes\mathrm{SL}_2(R)$, with
the linear action on $(u,v)$ and the identity on $z$.
The assignments (E.18.1), with the final central coordinate
changed from $2$ to $5$ and the matrices taken modulo nine,
define an epimorphism $\rho_{4,9}:B_4\to H_9$.
Its composition with reduction modulo three is precisely
$\widetilde\rho_4$ of E.18.

Let $\theta_i:F_2\to H_9$, $1\leq i\leq6$, be the
six actual evaluation maps of E.17. For
$B=C_2*C_3$, choose representatives $b_q$ of
$B/F_2\simeq\mathfrak S_3$ and set
\[
 K_6=N'N^6,\qquad
 K_{3,9}=K_6\cap
   \bigcap_{i=1}^6\bigcap_{q\in B/F_2}
       b_q^{-1}\ker(\theta_i)b_q,
 \qquad D_9=B/K_{3,9}.
 \tag{E.19.1}
\]
Thus $K_{3,9}$ is normal of finite index in $B$ and lies
in $F_2$. The kernel of $D_9\to G_6$ is
$\F_3^4$, and the image of $K_6\cap F_2'$ in that
kernel is $\F_3^3$.

For each of the 24 particular $G_6$ points retained in
E.17, all three commutator-correction parameters can be
solved simultaneously. The gentle norm equations have
rank two. The modulus-nine pentagon has rank three and
selects exactly one correction in this three-dimensional
image. The resulting literal words have zero integral
$F_2$-abelianization, satisfy both complete hexagons in
$D_9$, give surjective three-strand shadow maps, and
satisfy the complete pentagon in $H_9$. Their three
four-strand braid images satisfy all braid relations
and generate $H_9$.

This yields nonempty compatible finite tests for all
24 CM fibres. In this particular construction
$N'N^{18}\subset K_{3,9}$: the three-strand quotient
is an explicit quotient of $G_{18}$. The new condition
is the specified four-strand pentagon; no cofinal
extension follows from this statement.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Compatible extension through every relative quotient of order prime to six. In this statement $N=N_B$ is the rank-$97$ kernel of
$B=C_2*C_3\to Q$, and hats denote full profinite completions.
Let $\mathscr P$ be the set of primes other than two and three.
For each open subgroup $L\triangleleft\widehat B$ contained
in $\widehat N$ with $[\widehat N:L]$ prime to six, and
integers $a,b\geq1$, put
\[
 K_{a,b,L}=
 \bigl(\overline{\gamma_3N\,N^{2^a3^b}}\bigr)\cap L.
 \tag{E.20.1}
\]
Every one of the $24$ admissible CM matrix pairs has a
compatible family of gentle shadows at the inverse images
of these subgroups in $\widehat B_3$, with multiplier one.
The family is compatible as $a,b$ increase and as $L$
decreases, and its projection to every quotient
$B/(\gamma_3N\,N^j)$ in E.15 is the family constructed
there. In particular it
includes simultaneous refinement by arbitrary relative
pro-$p$ quotients for every $p\geq5$, of every nilpotency
class, and by finite relative kernels whose orders involve
several primes in $\mathscr P$.

Here the three-strand action is constructed on one actual
profinite quotient, together with a conjugator in the image
of $\widehat F_2'$. No extra pentagon assertion is made.
The natural map to the finite quotient
\[
 B/\bigl(\gamma_4N\,(\gamma_2N)^3N^9\bigr)
 \tag{E.20.2}
\]
factors through none of the quotients in (E.20.1).
Its normal kernel over $Q$ is a finite three-group with
a nonzero third lower-central term, exhibited below.
Thus (E.20.1) supplies further compatible refinements while
leaving this specified relative three-primary comparison.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
Complete compatible corrections in the fourth-degree Ferrari quotient. Let
\[
 \mathcal A_d=\F_3\langle X,Y\rangle/(\text{monomials of degree}>d),
 \qquad
 K_d=\langle1+X,1+Y\rangle\subset\mathcal A_d^\times.
\]
On the actual free generators $\xi_1,\xi_2$ of the
Ferrari kernel take the automorphisms
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 a:&\quad\xi_1\mapsto\xi_1,
           &&\xi_2\mapsto\xi_2\xi_1,\\
 b:&\quad\xi_1\mapsto\xi_1\xi_2^{-1},
           &&\xi_2\mapsto\xi_2.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{E.21.1}
\]
Their actual finite image on $K_d$ is denoted $C_d$.
The assignments
\[
 \sigma_1\mapsto(1,a),\qquad
 \sigma_2\mapsto(1,b),\qquad
 \sigma_3\mapsto(\xi_1,a)
 \tag{E.21.2}
\]
define an epimorphism $B_4\to K_d\rtimes C_d$.
Here the cubic powers are retained:
$(1+X)^3=1+X^3$ and $(1+Y)^3=1+Y^3$.

Let $T_4$ be the joint image of (E.21.2) for $d=4$
and the modulus-nine representation $\rho_{4,9}$
of E.19. Its reduction to the E.18 target is
surjective, with elementary abelian kernel
$\F_3^{12}$. Consequently
\[
 |T_4|=344373768,
 \qquad
 |B_4/(\ker(B_4\to T_4)\cap PB_4)|=8264970432.
 \tag{E.21.3}
\]

Form the three-strand core by the six evaluation
maps and all six $B/F_2$ conjugates, exactly as
in (E.19.1), now with target $T_4$, and intersect
it with $K_6$. Denote this kernel by $K_{3,4}$
and put $D_4=B/K_{3,4}$. Its kernel over $G_6$
has dimension seven over $\F_3$, the image of
$K_6\cap F_2'$ has dimension six, and the image
of $N'$ has dimension three.

For each of the 24 retained E.17 $G_6$ points,
the complete gentle norm equations on this
six-dimensional correction image have rank
four; the simultaneous pentagon in the two
targets has rank five. The combined system
is consistent of rank five, hence has an
affine line of corrections. An actual
commutator word in each line is retained.
It satisfies both complete hexagons in
$D_4$, gives a surjective three-strand
shadow, satisfies the full pentagon in
$T_4$, and defines a surjective four-strand
braid map to $T_4$. The three- and
four-strand full twists are preserved.

Thus all 24 CM fibres remain nonempty in
this joint finite test. In the specified
three-strand quotient, $\gamma_3N$ and
$N^{18}$ are killed. It therefore belongs
to the relative class-two coverage of
E.15; the new check is the displayed
four-strand constraint.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
A compatible relative class-three test preserving every retained CM point. Extend the actual Ferrari Magnus representation
(E.21.1)--(E.21.2) to $d=5$, retaining its joint
image $T_5$ with the modulus-nine target. Define
$K_{3,5}$ by all six evaluation maps, all six
$B/F_2$ conjugates, and intersection with $K_6$,
as in (E.19.1). Put $D_5=B/K_{3,5}$. The
specified reduction maps give
\[
 D_5\longrightarrow D_4\longrightarrow G_6,
 \qquad
 T_5\longrightarrow T_4\longrightarrow\widetilde H_3.
 \tag{E.22.1}
\]
The kernel of $D_5\to D_4$ is $\F_3^6$.
Its entire image is represented by words in
$K_{3,4}\cap F_2'$. The kernel of $D_5\to G_6$
has order $3^{13}$. The actual lower-central
images of $N$ in $D_5$ have dimensions
\[
 \dim\im(\gamma_2N)=9,\qquad
 \dim\im(\gamma_3N)=3,\qquad
 \im(\gamma_4N)=1,
 \tag{E.22.2}
\]
where the two nonzero images are elementary
abelian three-groups.

All three points of each of the 24 correction
lines in E.21 are included in the next test.
Every one of those 72 points has a gentle lift
to $D_5$. In each old line exactly one point
has a simultaneous pentagon lift; its top
correction is unique. Thus every one of the
24 particular E.17 $G_6$ shadows, including
all twelve extra-coset points, has a verified
compatible lift through (E.22.1). These
literal commutator words give surjective
three-strand shadows and surjective
four-strand braid maps satisfying the
complete pentagon in $T_5$.

The full target orders are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |T_5|&=6\,778\,308\,875\,544,\\
 |B_4/(\ker(B_4\to T_5)\cap PB_4)|
       &=162\,679\,413\,013\,056.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{E.22.3}
\]
The three- and four-strand full twists
are preserved. The multiplier calculation
is exhaustive over lifts of the retained
$G_6$ shadows: the exact cusp order in
$D_5$ is 72, so all compatible values
$\lambda\equiv1\pmod{72}$ and
$m=(\lambda-1)/2\equiv0\pmod{36}$
give exactly the same finite equations.
This does not enumerate other multiplier
residues or other $G_6$ points within a
CM matrix fibre.

The natural quotient $B\to D_5$ factors
through none of the finite quotients in
E.20.1. Thus this is a concrete relative
class-three extension beyond that family,
with positive witnesses in all 24 CM
fibres. It is one specified finite
refinement, with no all-quotient
lifting assertion.
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
A relative class-four refinement with complete correction planes. Extend the same actual Ferrari Magnus representation to
degree six, retaining its joint image $T_6$ with the
modulus-nine target. Let $K_{3,6}$ be the intersection
of $K_6$ with the kernels of all six evaluations and
all six $B/F_2$ conjugates, and put $D_6=B/K_{3,6}$.
The actual reduction maps are
\[
 D_6\longrightarrow D_5\longrightarrow G_6,
 \qquad T_6\longrightarrow T_5.
 \tag{E.23.1}
\]
The kernel of $D_6\to D_5$ is $\F_3^6$;
its whole image is represented by words in
$K_{3,5}\cap F_2'$. The kernel of $D_6\to G_6$
is elementary abelian of dimension 19.
The successive lower-central images of $N$ are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|rrrr}
 j&2&3&4&5\\\hline
 \dim\im(\gamma_jN)&15&6&3&0.
 \end{array}
 \tag{E.23.2}
\]
Thus this specified relative source quotient has
class four. Its natural map does not factor
through $D_5$, whose fourth-commutator image
is trivial by E.22.

Above each of E.22's 24 simultaneous points,
the entire next correction set is an affine
plane over $\F_3$. All nine points in each
plane are surjective gentle shadows and
satisfy the complete pentagon. All 216
associated four-strand triples generate
the whole target $T_6$ and preserve the
three- and four-strand full twists. In
particular all twelve extra-coset CM
fibres still have positive witnesses.

The exact target orders are
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |T_6|&=133\,417\,453\,597\,332\,552,\\
 |B_4/(\ker(B_4\to T_6)\cap PB_4)|
   &=3\,202\,018\,886\,335\,981\,248.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{E.23.3}
\]
The cusp period remains 72 in the source
joint quotient. Every multiplier lift
of the retained $G_6$ shadows therefore
has the same equations at this level,
as in E.22. This is the complete
comparison over the stated 24 points,
with all 216 surviving corrections
retained for further refinements.
No assertion of lifting through all
finite quotients follows from (E.23.1).
notes: Read the statement and proof for its exact scope; task-level completeness is recorded separately.

statement:
A complete joint binary and ternary Ferrari refinement. Use (E.21.1)--(E.21.2) in the actual algebra
\[
 \mathcal A_{2,d}=\F_2\langle X,Y\rangle/
                 (\text{monomials of degree}>d),
 \qquad 2\leq d\leq6,
 \tag{E.24.1}
\]
and denote the resulting four-strand target by
$T_{2,d}$. All square terms are retained.
Let $D_{2,6}$ be the three-strand quotient
formed by the six evaluations, their six
$B/F_2$ conjugates, and intersection with
$K_6$, exactly as in (E.19.1). Then
\[
 \ker(D_{2,6}\to G_6)\simeq\F_2^9,
 \qquad
 \im(K_6\cap F_2'\to D_{2,6})\simeq\F_2^7.
 \tag{E.24.2}
\]
The actual common source quotient with
E.23 is the fibre product
\[
 D_{2,6}\mathbin{\times_{G_6}}D_6,
 \tag{E.24.3}
\]
whose kernel over $G_6$ is
$\F_2^9\times\F_3^{19}$.

For every one of the 24 retained
$G_6$ points, all compatible multiplier
residues in (E.24.3) are $1,73$ modulo
144. For each residue the complete
binary correction system has an
affine line of two solutions.
Every one combines with every
point of E.23's nine-point ternary
plane by an actual $F_2'$ word.
Thus each retained CM fibre has
36 simultaneous points, for a
total of 864. All give surjective
three-strand shadows, satisfy both
complete target pentagons, and
give surjective four-strand braid
maps preserving the full twists
with the specified multiplier.
In particular every extra-coset
CM fibre survives this refinement.

The exact binary target order is
\[
 |T_{2,6}|=6\cdot2^{40}
          =6\,597\,069\,766\,656.
 \tag{E.24.4}
\]
The actual joint four-strand image
is $T_{2,6}\times T_6$. Its
kernel is already contained in
$PB_4$, and its order is
\[
 880\,164\,249\,471\,192\,366\,606\,672\,986\,112.
 \tag{E.24.5}
\]
These counts and comparisons concern
the entire finite correction fibres
over the specified $G_6$ points.
They do not enumerate other $G_6$
points or other initial multiplier
residues in a CM matrix fibre,
and do not assert full profinite
lifting.

statement:
The complete joint quartic distribution test. Keep $B,F,N_B,G_6$ and the twenty-four retained words $f_i\in F'$
of E.1, indexed $i=0,\ldots,23$ in the saved certificate order.
Let $q_{24}:F\to\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z/24)$ send
\[
 x\longmapsto U^2=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad y\longmapsto W^2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{E.25.1}
\]
Put $\mathcal N=\{2,3,4,6,12\}$ and retain every coefficient
$c_N$ of D.5 modulo twelve.  For each $i$, the complete set of
pairs $(c_2,c_3)\in(\mathbb Z/12)^2$ attained by words
$f_i k$, $k\in N_B'$, satisfying simultaneously
\[
\begin{gathered}
 q_{24}\delta_N(f_i k)=q_{24}(y)^{c_N(f_i k)}q_{24}(f_i k)
       \quad(N\in\mathcal N),\\
 c_4=2c_2,\qquad c_6=c_2+c_3,\qquad c_{12}=2c_2+c_3
       \pmod {12}
\end{gathered}
 \tag{E.25.2}
\]
is exactly $\{a_i\}\times\mathbb Z/12$, where
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (a_0,\ldots,a_{11})&=(0,6,0,6,6,0,6,0,4,10,4,10),\\
 (a_{12},\ldots,a_{23})&=(10,4,10,8,4,10,4,10,4,10,4,10).
\end{aligned}
 \tag{E.25.3}
\]
For the auxiliary image allowing every correction in
$K_6=N_B'N_B^6$, the exact set is
$\{a_i,a_i+6\}\times\mathbb Z/12$.
The latter calculation does not impose an additional $F'$ condition
on that larger correction group; the former already supplies actual
words in $F'$ with unchanged $G_6$ image.

The joint correction images of $N_B'$ and $K_6$ have orders
\[
             2\,717\,908\,992,
       \qquad65\,229\,815\,808,
 \tag{E.25.4}
\]
respectively.  Thus all twelve retained CM-compatible points and
all twelve retained extra points pass this joint test.  Each admits
every value of $\rho_3=-c_3\pmod4$; restricting both $c_2,c_3$ to
even residues still leaves both values $0,2$ of $\rho_3\pmod4$.
This assertion concerns exactly the finite identities (E.25.2).
It asserts neither generation in their induced cover quotient nor
a full profinite GT realization.

statement:
The exact Fermat proper-Tate quotient and its boundary refinement. Start with the discrete group $B=C_2*C_3$.  Use the literal
level-two generators of the E.1 verifier,
$x=(r^{-1}s)^2=(sr)^{-2}$ and $y=(sr^{-1})^2=sxs$.
Let $F=\langle x,y\rangle\triangleleft B$, and put
\[
 H=\ker(F\to(\mathbb Z/3)^2),\qquad
 T=H^{\rm ab}/\langle\text{the nine cusp classes}\rangle.
 \tag{E.26.1}
\]
The based cubic cover identifies $H$ with the topological
fundamental group of the punctured Fermat cubic, and
$T\simeq\mathbb Z^2$ is its proper integral homology lattice.
After profinite completion the corresponding finite cover
identifies $\widehat H$ with the geometric \'etale fundamental
group, and $\widehat T=\varprojlim_m T/mT$
with the full Tate module of its smooth compactification.
For $m\ge1$, set $J_m=\ker(H\to T/mT)$; it is normal in $B$.
There are actual quotient maps
\[
       B\longrightarrow G_{3m}\longrightarrow B/J_m.
 \tag{E.26.2}
\]
In particular every proper two-power Tate quotient of this
specified cover is dominated by the homology tower of E.4.
The inverse-limit comparison is the surjection
\[
       \widehat B/\overline{[N_B,N_B]}
            \longrightarrow\varprojlim_m B/J_m.
 \tag{E.26.3}
\]
These statements retain the intrinsic Fermat curve and its
based maps; no CM twist comparison is implicit in them.

The full rank-ten homology quotient
$B/[H,H]H^4$ gives additional information.  In the ordered
basis $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_{10}$ specified below, the first two
literal $N_B$ generators satisfy
\[
 [n_1,n_2]\longmapsto2\eta_3-2\eta_{10}\ne0
            \quad\hbox{in }H^{\rm ab}/4,
 \tag{E.26.4}
\]
where $n_1=y^6$ and $n_2=yx^{-1}yx^{-2}yx^{-1}y$.
Consequently the actual common refinement
\[
     B/(K_6\cap[H,H]H^4)\longrightarrow G_6
 \tag{E.26.5}
\]
cannot be dominated by any $G_j$ through the specified maps
from $B$.

statement:
The generating-pair \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} Ferrari quotient and its exact source factor. Let $\mathcal P$ be the set of all eighteen ordered generating pairs of
$S_3$, and let
\[
 K=\im\bigl(\langle\xi_1,\xi_2\rangle\longrightarrow S_3^{\mathcal P}\bigr),
 \qquad \xi_1\longmapsto(g)_{(g,h)},\quad
 \xi_2\longmapsto(h)_{(g,h)}.
 \tag{E.27.1}
\]
The literal Ferrari Nielsen automorphisms in E.17 permute $\mathcal P$.
Their image $A\leq\operatorname{Aut}(K)$ has order $162$, and the resulting
four-strand quotient $T=K\rtimes A$ has order $17\,496$.
The free image has order $108$ and
\[
 [K,K]=\gamma_3(K)\simeq(\mathbb Z/3)^3.
 \tag{E.27.2}
\]
In particular $K$ is nonnilpotent.

For the six pure evaluation pairs of E.17, both entries have order
three and the two entries commute. Consequently their evaluations
kill $F'$. Their common induced six-coset source map is exactly a
faithful representation of
\[
 B/(F'F^3),\qquad |B/(F'F^3)|=54,
 \tag{E.27.3}
\]
where $F\triangleleft B=C_2*C_3$ is the free subgroup of index six
used throughout Part E. Since $K_6=N'N^6\subset F'F^3$, its reduction
from $G_6$ is the specified quotient homomorphism
\[
 B\longrightarrow G_6\longrightarrow B/(F'F^3).
 \tag{E.27.4}
\]
Every $f\in\widehat F'$ has six identity values in $T$. For every
profinite unit multiplier, the resulting four-strand braid map is
surjective and preserves the two full twists with that multiplier.
In particular all twenty-four retained $G_6$ points of E.17, and
every lift of those points used in E.24, pass this finite test.

statement:
The complete two-adic boundary tower and its joint Ferrari lifts. Keep the discrete groups and the ten-generator integral basis of E.26.
Put
\[
 M_H=H^{\rm ab},\qquad
 B_n=B/[H,H]H^{2^n},\qquad
 C_n=B/(K_6\cap[H,H]H^{2^n})\quad(n\ge1).
 \tag{E.28.1}
\]
Every one of the twenty-four retained $G_6$ words $f_i$ admits an
explicit correction in $N_B'$ giving compatible multiplier-one
automorphisms of every $C_n$.  One integral correcting word works
at all these levels.  The complete set of correction images in
$M_H/2^n$ coming from $N_B'$ and satisfying both hexagons has
exactly $2^n$ elements; every one is generating.  Its inverse
limit is an affine copy of $\mathbb Z_2$.

Let $\mathscr D=D_{2,6}\times_{G_6}D_6$ be the exact source
quotient of E.24.  Each of the eighteen multiplier-one points
in each of E.24's twenty-four indexed CM families extends
through the entire common tower
\[
 \mathscr C_n=\operatorname{im}
       \bigl(B\longrightarrow\mathscr D\times B_n\bigr).
 \tag{E.28.2}
\]
Thus all $432$ multiplier-one points of E.24 are retained
simultaneously with this tower.  The same single profinite
commutator word gives these compatible lifts and leaves unchanged
all six binary and all six ternary Ferrari evaluations, their
induced conjugate coordinates, both pentagons, and the generating
four-strand maps of E.24.

This tower retains commutators at every relative lower-central
depth.  If $P_n$ is the image of $N_B$ in $B_n$, then there is an
explicit primitive rank-six lattice $\mathcal D\subset M_H$ such
that
\[
 \gamma_r(P_n)=\mathcal D/2^n\mathcal D
            \simeq(\mathbb Z/2^n)^6
       \qquad(r\ge2).
 \tag{E.28.3}
\]
Consequently no quotient of $B$ with nilpotent image of $N_B$
dominates $B_n$ through the specified maps.  The assertion is
about the displayed common towers and finite Ferrari tests;
it makes no full-GT realization assertion.

statement:
All retained fibres survive the complete $A_5$ Ferrari test. Let $D_{23}$ be the actual joint three-strand source quotient of
E.24, and let $T_{23}=T_{2,6}\times T_{3,6}$ be its actual
four-strand target. We retain all $432$ multiplier-one points
of E.24, including both binary corrections and every point
of each ternary plane.

There is an explicit finite Ferrari quotient
$\pi_A:B_4\twoheadrightarrow T_A$ whose free Ferrari kernel is
$A_5^{19}$. Its associated six-evaluation, six-coset induced
homomorphism is $\rho_A:B=C_2*C_3\twoheadrightarrow G_A$.
Every one of the $432$ points has a correction in $N'$ that
preserves its complete $D_{23}$ image and satisfies both
hexagons and the full pentagon in the common refinement with
$G_A$ and $T_A$. The resulting three-strand map and the map
onto the actual joint four-strand image are surjective.
In particular, all $24$ retained CM fibres, including all
$12$ extra fibres, survive this nonsolvable finite test.
